title: TS-OOD: Evaluating Time-Series Out-of-Distribution Detection and Prospective Directions
relevance_component: most OOD methods fail on time series
takeaway: Comprehensive benchmark: MOST SOTA OOD-detection methods (developed for vision/NLP) perform POORLY on multivariate time series; deep-feature-modeling OOD methods do better. Direct #14 warning for TRINETRA: you CANNOT lift an off-the-shelf vision OOD detector onto sensor streams and expect it to flag novel hazard regimes - OOD on time series is an open problem needing time-series-specific (deep-feature) methods, validated per-modality. OOD misses produce 'confidently wrong' alarms (the paper's exact failure mode), the drift/novelty surface #14.

title: Learning Hyperspherical Time-Frequency Representations for Time-Series OOD Detection
relevance_component: time-freq hyperspherical OOD embeddings
takeaway: Formulates time-series OOD as representation learning with hyperspherical (von Mises-Fisher) class-conditional embeddings over time-frequency features; principled detection under distributional shift. For TRINETRA #14: a concrete SOTA technique (time-frequency + hyperspherical) to build a sensor-stream OOD detector that flags novel/unseen hazard dynamics before the forecaster emits a confident-but-wrong output; complements TS-OOD. Ties the Deep-SVDD hypersphere theme (2108.04907) - same geometric family.

title: Toward Sustainable Subterranean mMTC: Space-Air-Ground-Underground Networks Powered by LoRaWAN and WET
relevance_component: LoRaWAN SF/airtime/energy under harsh coverage
takeaway: Space-Air-Ground-Underground integrated net using LoRaWAN + wireless energy transfer for remote/disaster/hard-to-reach monitoring; simulations show spread-factor (SF) choice, reporting period, and time-allocation critically determine coverage, lifetime and feasibility. For TRINETRA LoRa layer (#6/#10): quantifies the SF vs airtime vs energy vs coverage trade-off the BOM glosses - a wrong SF either kills range (misses nodes) or blows duty-cycle/energy budget; also a satellite-backhaul option for valleys with no terrestrial gateway.

title: Energy Efficiency Optimization for Subterranean LoRaWAN Using RL (Direct-to-Satellite)
relevance_component: co-SF interference + RL SF allocation
takeaway: In DENSE LoRaWAN, assigning quasi-orthogonal spreading factors to minimise co-SF interference is hard; multi-agent RL (MAD3QN/MAA2C) allocates SFs for energy efficiency, beating 4 benchmarks. For TRINETRA: during a disaster MANY nodes transmit at once (correlated alarm traffic) -> co-SF interference + collisions spike exactly when reliability matters most; the architecture assumes benign LoRa capacity. Flags a capacity/collision failure mode under disaster load (extends #6/#10).

title: On Extending the Wireless Communications Range of Weather Stations using LoRaWAN
relevance_component: low-cost LoRaWAN weather relay, dev-country
takeaway: Low-cost/low-power device decodes consumer weather-station data and relays it over LoRaWAN, extending ~100 m range for disaster prevention in developing countries (ICTP/ITU). For TRINETRA: a direct cheap precedent for the ground weather/rain-gauge relay (same ₹2000 ethos); supports BOM feasibility but underscores the ~100 m native range forcing LoRa relaying (link-budget realism, #10).

title: WaveDINO: Learning-Based Atmospheric Correction of Unwrapped InSAR Interferograms Validated by GNSS
relevance_component: DL atmospheric correction beats weather models
takeaway: InSAR deformation is corrupted by atmospheric phase delay, seasonal change, decorrelation; numerical-weather-model corrections leave residual bias. WaveDINO = wavelet multi-scale denoiser conditioned on frozen DINOv3 features + terrain, trained on synthetic deformation + real atmospheric noise; cuts GNSS misfit ~3%/19% at two volcanoes, beating weather-model corrections. CRITICAL #1/#3 input integrity: TRINETRA's datacube assumes clean unwrapped phase, but Himalayan tropospheric/seasonal delay is severe and will masquerade as deformation -> false landslide signal into the physics gate. Learned + GNSS-validated atmospheric correction is a REQUIRED preprocessing stage the pipeline omits.

title: A deep learning approach to detecting volcano deformation from satellite imagery using synthetic datasets
relevance_component: synthetic-data training for rare deformation
takeaway: Only a tiny fraction of targets deform and atmospheric noise is ubiquitous -> extreme class imbalance for InSAR deformation detection; trains AlexNet on SYNTHETIC interferograms (analytic deformation + stratified + turbulent atmospheric noise), beating training on real data alone, final PPV 82% after adding real examples; atmospheric correction applied only to the small positive subset to save compute. For TRINETRA #11/#1: a proven recipe for the rare-event problem (synthetic physics-based augmentation to beat imbalance) + the pragmatic 'correct atmosphere only on positives' compute trick. Strong #18 benchmark, directly transferable to landslide deformation.

title: Hybrid Value Estimation for Off-policy Evaluation and Offline Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: bias-variance OPE value estimation
takeaway: Hybrid Value Estimation trades off bias/variance by blending value estimates from offline data and a learned model, better error bound than direct methods; gives OPHVE (off-policy eval) + MOHVE (offline RL). For TRINETRA RL alarm policy (#9/#11): before deploying any offline-learned alarm policy you MUST evaluate it off-policy on logged data; naive OPE has high variance (few disaster episodes), so a hybrid model+data estimator is the right tool to certify the policy without live trials. Supports an honest OPE gate the report lacks.

title: Offline RL Without Off-Policy Evaluation (One-Step)
relevance_component: one-step beats iterative; OPE variance
takeaway: Shows ONE step of constrained/regularized policy improvement using an on-policy Q of the behavior policy beats iterative actor-critic on much of D4RL, while being simpler + more hyperparameter-robust; argues iterative offline RL suffers high-variance repeated OPE. For TRINETRA #9: its offline CQL/IQL stage is iterative and data-poor (few disasters) -> high-variance, fragile; a one-step baseline is a simpler more robust alternative to benchmark first (Occam + #18). Tempers the multi-stage RL complexity.

title: Socio-meteorology: flood prediction social preparedness and cry wolf effects
relevance_component: cry-wolf: false alarms destroy trust & preparedness
takeaway: Builds a socio-hydrological model coupling flood, social collective MEMORY, collective TRUST in the warning system, and preparedness actions; realistically reproduces the CRY-WOLF effect (many false alarms undermine credibility and suppress preparedness). Two key findings for TRINETRA: (1) trust dynamics matter MORE in low-frequency-disaster regions (exactly the Himalaya's rare catastrophic events) than high-frequency ones; (2) as forecast skill improves, system efficiency becomes MORE sensitive to social trust, so the warning THRESHOLD must be set accounting for social response, not just statistical cost. This is the missing social half of the #1 threshold bug and the #9 FA-penalty: a FA is not merely -5 reward, it degrades future compliance - the RL/threshold design must internalise trust erosion. Strong decision-layer finding (ties new candidate #8 compliance).

title: Governance-Constrained Agentic AI: Blockchain-Enforced Human Oversight for Safety-Critical Wildfire Monitoring
relevance_component: human-in-loop oversight for autonomous alerts
takeaway: Argues purely AUTONOMOUS alert dissemination in safety-critical disasters risks false-alarming, governance failure, and lack of verifiable responsibility; proposes structurally-defined human control + cryptographically-verifiable accountability over the AI monitoring agents. For TRINETRA #0/#9: directly relevant to the workflow-faked-success failure (#0) and the autonomous RL alarm policy - a safety-critical EWS needs auditable human-in-the-loop gates and tamper-evident provenance, not fully-autonomous dissemination. Supports an accountability/oversight layer the architecture lacks (and a counterpoint: don't over-engineer with blockchain). Governance template for the decision layer.

title: Routing-Free Mixture-of-Experts
relevance_component: eliminates router/TopK/load-balance instability
takeaway: Standard MoE routers impose rigid inductive bias + need load-balancing hacks; Routing-Free MoE removes external routers/Softmax/Top-K/load-balancing, letting each expert self-activate via continuous gradient flow with a unified adaptive balancing framework; better scalability + robustness. For TRINETRA GMF (gated MoE head): a warning that hard Top-K routing is brittle and a candidate design to avoid routing-collapse where one expert dominates (relevant to the stacked-head stability concern + 2601.03425 'standing committee'); supports a soft, self-activating expert mix for the fusion head.

title: The Illusion of Specialization: Domain-Invariant Standing Committee in Mixture-of-Experts
relevance_component: MoE routing collapses to a fixed expert coalition
takeaway: COMMITTEEAUDIT shows MoE models do NOT achieve the assumed domain specialization: a compact domain-INVARIANT 'standing committee' of experts captures most routing mass across domains/layers/budgets. Direct caution for TRINETRA's GMF: assuming each expert specializes to a hazard modality (InSAR vs rain vs river) is likely FALSE - routing may collapse onto a few experts regardless of input, defeating the reliability-gating goal. Must AUDIT expert utilisation + enforce/verify genuine specialization, else the 'expert per modality' story is illusory (#18 honesty + GMF design).

title: Stacked Generalizations in Imbalanced Fraud Data Sets using Resampling Methods
relevance_component: stacking + resampling under imbalance
takeaway: Two-step stacked generalization (base learners -> meta/super learner) improves over individuals especially when combined with resampling on heavily IMBALANCED data; weakest base learners improve most; essentially enhanced cross-validation but compute-heavy. For TRINETRA GMF + rare-event hazards (#11/#1): empirical support that stacking helps under extreme imbalance IF paired with proper resampling and rigorous CV, but at high compute cost - informs the meta-head training protocol and warns that stacking without imbalance handling won't help the rare-disaster regime.

title: The super learner for time-to-event outcomes: A tutorial
relevance_component: super-learner theory: oracle, CV ensemble
takeaway: Tutorial on the SUPER LEARNER (van der Laan): a cross-validation-based ensemble with an oracle property - asymptotically performs as well as the best candidate (or combination) in a pre-specified library, here for censored time-to-event risk estimation. For TRINETRA GMF: the theoretical foundation for why a stacked meta-head is principled (oracle guarantee via honest CV), AND the discipline it demands - a pre-specified library + proper cross-validation to avoid overfitting the meta-learner. Time-to-event framing also maps onto 'time-to-failure' hazard forecasting (Fukuzono/Voight inverse-velocity). Grounds the GMF novelty claim in established theory (#16/#18).

title: Auto-differentiable Ensemble Kalman Filters
relevance_component: EnKF + ML to learn unknown dynamics
takeaway: AD-EnKF blends ensemble Kalman filtering (scales to high-dim state recovery) with automatic differentiation to train surrogate models of UNKNOWN dynamics; beats EM/particle-filter hybrids on Lorenz-96, easy to implement. For TRINETRA physics layer: a principled route to ASSIMILATE sparse noisy sensor observations into the slope-hydrology/infiltration state (Iverson/Richards) while learning the parts of the dynamics the physics model omits - i.e., sequential state estimation + uncertainty for the physics gate, instead of a static one-shot FS computation. Candidate upgrade to make the physics gate a filtered, uncertainty-aware state estimator (#3/#17).

title: Long-time accuracy of ensemble Kalman filters for chaotic and machine-learned dynamical systems
relevance_component: EnKF long-horizon error bounds; ML-surrogate caveat
takeaway: Establishes conditions under which EnKF estimation error stays small over LONG horizons for partially-observed chaotic systems (Navier-Stokes, Lorenz), including with ML surrogate dynamics. For TRINETRA: if the physics gate uses sequential assimilation (per 2107.07687), this gives the theoretical guardrails for when it stays accurate over a long monitoring deployment vs when a learned surrogate will drift - directly relevant to the drift/long-run-stability surface (#14) and to trusting the physics state during extended quiescent periods between rare events.

title: On the Relationship Between Interpretability and Explainability in Machine Learning
relevance_component: interpretability vs explainability are complementary
takeaway: Position paper: interpretability (inherently-readable models) and explainability (post-hoc explanations of black boxes) are NOT substitutes - each mitigates the other's shortcomings, and high-stakes decisions need both. For TRINETRA: an evacuation alarm is a high-stakes decision requiring human trust; the GMF black-box meta-head needs post-hoc explanation AND the physics gate provides intrinsic interpretability - the report should pair them, not rely on one. Grounds a requirement for explainable alarm justification (feeds trust/compliance, ties cry-wolf 2104.11422).

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence Approaches: A Survey
relevance_component: XAI method taxonomy for high-stakes adoption
takeaway: Survey of XAI methods (local/global, model-agnostic/specific) and the open challenge that black-box opacity blocks AI adoption in high-stakes domains; recommends paths to human-centred AI. For TRINETRA: a catalogue to choose explanation methods (SHAP/attention/counterfactual) for the alarm head so disaster managers can audit WHY an alarm fired - essential for the governance/oversight layer (ties 2604.04265) and regulatory acceptance of SACHET/CAP alerts.

title: DLTTA: Dynamic Learning Rate for Test-time Adaptation on Cross-domain Medical Images
authors: Yang; Chen; Jiang; Liu; Cao; Heng; Dou
relevance_component: per-sample dynamic LR test-time adaptation
takeaway: Test-time adaptation with a FIXED learning rate is sub-optimal because the scale of distribution shift changes as data arrives sequentially; DLTTA uses a memory-bank discrepancy estimate to modulate per-sample weight updates, improving over SOTA TTA on 3 medical tasks. For TRINETRA #14: a model deployed across Uttarakhand+Himachal faces continuous cross-region/seasonal shift; naive TTA could destabilise a safety-critical forecaster - DLTTA shows adaptation strength must be gated by measured shift. BUT also a caution: unsupervised TTA on a life-safety model is risky (could adapt toward wrong pseudo-labels), reinforcing need for the conformal/abstention guardrails (#13).

title: Label Distribution Shift-Aware Prediction Refinement for Test-Time Adaptation (DART)
relevance_component: detect+correct test-time label-distribution shift
takeaway: DART detects and corrects CLASS/LABEL distribution shift at test time, improving pseudo-label accuracy by 5-18% under label shift on CIFAR-10C and with NO degradation when no shift exists; a plug-in to existing TTA. For TRINETRA #14/#11: hazard class priors shift drastically between calm periods and monsoon/event onset (label-distribution shift); a detector that corrects for this without harming the no-shift case is exactly the guardrail an always-on alarm system needs to avoid prior-induced miscalibration - and the 'no degradation when no shift' property is the safety-preserving design pattern.

title: Diffusion-Based Probabilistic Modeling for Hourly Streamflow Prediction and Assimilation (h-Diffusion)
relevance_component: hourly probabilistic streamflow + data assimilation
takeaway: HOURLY flood peaks are distinctly higher than daily - critical for warnings; MTS-LSTM lacks probabilistic forecasts/assimilation. h-Diffusion (denoising diffusion) conditions on observed/simulated daily discharge to generate hourly hydrographs, beats MTS-LSTM/MF-LSTM on CAMELS-hourly esp. on EXTREME metrics, and uses inpainting to assimilate recent observations. For TRINETRA flash-flood layer (#8): directly relevant - sub-daily resolution + probabilistic + observation assimilation is exactly what a flash-flood/River-Eye alarm needs; a SOTA baseline the report must benchmark against, and the diffusion+inpainting assimilation pattern complements the EnKF idea (2107.07687).

title: HydroDiffusion: Diffusion-Based Probabilistic Streamflow Forecasting with a State Space Backbone
relevance_component: diffusion + state-space long-range streamflow
takeaway: Improves on LSTM-backbone diffusion streamflow models (single-step objectives, poor long-range) with a STATE-SPACE (Mamba-style) backbone for coherent multi-lead probabilistic forecast trajectories + strong early flood-warning skill. For TRINETRA: a newer SOTA flash-flood forecasting comparator (state-space > LSTM for long-range dependencies) - relevant to lead-time maximisation in the RL reward and to building the flood expert in the GMF; reinforces that the report's flood module must be benchmarked against diffusion+SSM, not just LSTM.

title: Value of Information Aware Opportunistic Duty Cycling in Solar Harvesting Sensor Networks
relevance_component: VoI-driven duty cycling under stochastic harvested energy
takeaway: Solar-harvested WSNs cannot sustain FULL duty cycle on limited harvested energy, so they must operate at PARTIAL duty cycle and prioritise high-Value-of-Information data; the paper maps this to a budget-dynamic Multi-Arm Bandit over sampling/transmit/receive power states under stochastic energy + variable data importance. For TRINETRA ground IoT (#8/#10): the ₹2000 solar-powered LoRa nodes face exactly this - they CANNOT transmit continuously, so a VoI-aware policy must decide when to wake/sense/send, prioritising hazard-relevant data during storms (when solar is lowest!). The BOM/architecture assumes always-on sensing; this is a real energy-vs-coverage failure mode and gives the MAB framing to fix it.

title: Real-time Earthquake Early Warning with Deep Learning: 2016 Central Apennines Italy
relevance_component: FCN EEW: location+magnitude 4s after P
takeaway: Fully-convolutional net detects earthquakes + estimates location/magnitude from continuous waveform streams as soon as ONE station triggers, evolutionarily refining; on 2016 Mw6.0 Apennines, reliable within 4s of earliest P phase (6.8-3.7 km, 0.31-0.23 mag error). For TRINETRA Bug #7 (Chamoli needed a geophone NOT in the BOM): quantifies what a seismic early-warning channel delivers and how fast - evidence that for co-seismic landslide/rockfall triggers (Chamoli-type), a seismic sensor + DL gives seconds of lead the current satellite/IoT stack cannot; strengthens the #7 argument that omitting seismic is a real gap, and shows single-station DL EEW is feasible/cheap enough to add.

title: High Magnitude Earthquake Identification Using Anomaly Detection on HR GNSS Data (DetEQ)
authors: Quintero Arenas; Quinteros Cartaya; Padilla Lafarga; Moraila; Faber; Koehler; Srivastava
relevance_component: GNSS autoencoder anomaly-detection EEW + FP filtering
takeaway: DetEQ = lightweight CUSTOMIZABLE autoencoder pipeline detecting high-magnitude earthquakes as ANOMALIES in high-rate GNSS data: (i) anomaly score from reconstruction error, (ii) threshold detection, (iii) explicit FILTERING of local events to suppress false positives; trained on noise from 9 Chile stations, validated on 2011 Mw6.8 Concepcion. For TRINETRA #7/#1/#9: the SAME GNSS stream TRINETRA plans (2301.05977) can double as a co-seismic trigger via a cheap autoencoder - partially answering #7 'no geophone' gap WITHOUT new hardware; its stage-(iii) false-positive filtering is a design pattern for the anomaly layer, and reconstruction-error anomaly scoring mirrors TRINETRA's forecast-residual approach. Strong, directly transferable.

title: Measurement Optimization under Uncertainty using Deep Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: RL sensor placement maximising info gain
takeaway: Deterministic optimal-sensor-placement is insufficient under input/parameter uncertainty; formulates placement as an MDP where an RL agent places heterogeneous sensors to maximise an information-theoretic reward, demonstrated on a shear-building model. For TRINETRA: the ₹2000 node network across 110,000 km² needs principled PLACEMENT (which valleys/slopes get a node) - this gives an uncertainty-aware, information-maximising method to site the limited sensors where they most reduce hazard uncertainty, a design question the report leaves ad hoc (ties coverage realism #8/#10).

title: Efficient Sensor Placement from Regression with Sparse Gaussian Processes in Continuous and Discrete Spaces
relevance_component: scalable GP mutual-information sensor placement
takeaway: Classic MI-based sensor placement requires discretising the environment (cost scales with grid size), limiting scale; proposes a sparse-GP variational formulation optimisable by gradient descent in continuous domains, scaling to large problems for monitoring correlated phenomena (temperature/precipitation/salinity explicitly). For TRINETRA: a SCALABLE method to place rain/soil/tilt sensors across a huge continuous mountain domain to maximise coverage of correlated hazard fields - directly addresses siting the sparse ₹2000 network efficiently; more scalable complement to the RL approach (2303.09750).

title: AscDAMs: Advanced SLAM-based channel detection and mapping system
authors: Wang; Lu; Qin; Huang; Kong; Shen
relevance_component: SLAM channel mapping for debris-flow gullies
takeaway: High-resolution channel topography/deposit conditions are the prior challenge for channelized debris-flow study; satellite/drone struggle to see interior of long-deep gullies (Wenchuan region); SLAM fails there due to atypical features + violent sensor sway; AscDAMs post-processes SLAM (orthophoto deviation correction + point-cloud smoothing + cross-section extraction) for quantitative deposit/volume/change assessment before/after rainy season. For TRINETRA runout/debris-flow modelling (#11/#15): channel geometry + erodible deposit volume are KEY inputs to Scheidegger/Froehlich runout and SCS-CN, and this shows how hard they are to measure in exactly TRINETRA's terrain - the runout parameters feeding the physics gate carry large unmodeled geometric uncertainty (grounds a runout-input-uncertainty caveat).

title: A Protocol for Self-Synchronized Duty-Cycling in Sensor Networks (Wiselib)
authors: Hernandez; Baumgartner; Blesa; Blum; Kroller; Fekete
relevance_component: self-synchronized robust duty-cycling
takeaway: Self-synchronized duty-cycling protocol for energy-harvesting WSNs (Wiselib/Shawn, real iSense hardware specs); adapts to changing energy availability and is robust against packet loss. For TRINETRA #10: a concrete, hardware-validated protocol pattern for coordinating when a mesh of harvested nodes wakes/sleeps so the network stays synchronized + resilient to lost packets - the kind of MAC/duty-cycle layer the architecture assumes but doesn't specify; robustness-to-packet-loss is critical during disaster RF congestion.

title: Generalized Neural Networks for Real-Time Earthquake Early Warning
relevance_component: generalized EEW nets, 4s, cross-region
takeaway: Generalized neural networks for real-time EEW report location+magnitude within 4s of first triggered station across Japan + California (2.6-6.3 km, 0.05-0.17 mag error), eliminating complex empirical configurations and enabling GLOBAL application. For TRINETRA #7/#14: shows a seismic EWS net GENERALIZES across tectonic regions (relevant to Himalaya transfer where local training data is scarce) - supports both the 'add seismic' argument (#7) and the cross-region generalization need (#14); a strong external benchmark for any fast-trigger module.

title: Safe Probabilistic Planning for Human-Robot Interaction using Conformal Risk Control
relevance_component: CBF + conformal risk control = formal safety margins
takeaway: Combines control barrier functions (CBFs) with CONFORMAL RISK CONTROL to give formal probabilistic constraint-satisfaction guarantees while handling complex (human) behaviour; an algorithm dynamically adjusts conformal safety margins by interaction context; cuts collision/safety-violation rates vs baselines while keeping goal success. For TRINETRA #6/#7/#13: this is the exact template to make the safety SHIELD rigorous - replace ad-hoc hard thresholds with CBF-style constraints whose margins are conformally calibrated to a target violation probability, and ADAPT the margin to context (monsoon vs dry). Directly upgrades the shield + fixes the #13 conformal overclaim by tying coverage to a controlled risk, not just marginal coverage. SOTA-grounding for the shield design.

title: Selective Conformal Risk Control (SCRC)
relevance_component: conformal prediction + selective abstention, two-stage
takeaway: Conformal prediction gives distribution-free coverage but often oversized sets; SCRC integrates it with SELECTIVE CLASSIFICATION in two stages: (1) select confident samples, (2) apply conformal risk control on the selected subset for calibrated sets; SCRC-T preserves exchangeability (exact finite-sample guarantee), a second variant trades it off. For TRINETRA #13: directly addresses the conformal OVERCLAIM - the honest design is to ABSTAIN on low-confidence inputs (defer to physics gate / human) and only emit calibrated risk-controlled sets where confident, rather than claiming blanket coverage. Marries conformal + selective prediction (ties 2211.xxxx selective-prediction axis). The principled fix for the conformal module.

title: Evaluating Uncertainty in Deep Gaussian Processes
relevance_component: DGP/DSPP calibration under shift vs deep ensembles
takeaway: Evaluates Deep Gaussian Processes + Deep Sigma Point Processes for UQ calibration and robustness UNDER DISTRIBUTION SHIFT vs Deep Ensembles, on regression (CASP) + classification (ESR). For TRINETRA #8/#14: the calibrated people-at-risk estimate needs UQ that stays calibrated as conditions drift (monsoon/region shift); this benchmarks whether Bayesian DGP approaches actually beat the simpler Deep Ensemble baseline under shift - informs the choice of UQ backbone for the risk estimator and warns that fancier UQ is not automatically better-calibrated under shift.

title: Modeling spatial asymmetries in teleconnected extreme temperatures
relevance_component: DL+EVT for rare multivariate extremes, data-hungry caveat
takeaway: Combines deep generative models with extreme-value theory for the full multivariate distribution of extreme winter temperatures; EXPLICITLY notes that by definition extreme events are FEW, which limits data-hungry nonparametric NNs; DL beats vine-copulas at reproducing spatial asymmetries/extent of ERA5 extremes. For TRINETRA #11/#1: the core rare-event problem - DL struggles precisely where it matters (the tail), motivating EVT-informed modelling of hazard extremes rather than pure data-driven nets; a methodological warning + remedy for the extreme-precipitation/landslide tail the system must not miss.

title: Advancing Heatwave Forecasting via Distribution-Informed Graph Neural Networks (DI-GNNs): Integrating EVT with GNNs
relevance_component: EVT-informed GNN for rare extreme forecasting
takeaway: DI-GNN integrates extreme-value theory INTO a graph neural network to forecast rare heatwaves (1-15 day scale), tackling non-linear atmospheric interactions + rarity where heuristic-feature models fail to generalize across climates. For TRINETRA #11/#14: a concrete architecture pattern for baking tail-distribution structure into a spatial (graph) forecaster - transferable to spatially-correlated landslide/cloudburst extremes across the Himalayan network; addresses both rarity AND cross-climate generalization, two named TRINETRA weaknesses. Pairs with 2310.03220 as the EVT-into-DL evidence base.

title: NowcastDiT: Diffusion Transformers are Effective Precipitation Nowcasters
authors: Xu; Guo; Zhang; Zhong; Wang; Long
relevance_component: standard DiT + RL rewards SOTA precip nowcasting
takeaway: A STANDARD Diffusion Transformer is a simple scalable foundation for precipitation nowcasting; NowcastDiT adds a dynamics-aware noise prior (temporal coherence) + end-to-end RL with timestep-aware rewards for meteorological skill; SOTA on SEVIR + MRMS in both perceptual quality and skill. For TRINETRA #1: a current SOTA rainfall-nowcasting baseline the system must benchmark its precip input against; notably it uses RL-with-skill-rewards INSIDE the forecaster (echoing TRINETRA's RL alarm policy) and shows a plain DiT suffices - cautioning against over-specialized architectures (ties MoE 'standing committee' 2601.03425).

title: CasCast: Skillful High-resolution Precipitation Nowcasting via Cascaded Modelling
authors: Gong; Bai; Ye; Xu; Liu; Dai; Yang; Ouyang
relevance_component: cascaded framework for extreme-precip nowcasting
takeaway: CasCast tackles two unsolved nowcasting challenges: (i) multi-scale precipitation-system evolution and (ii) accurate forecasts for EXTREME precipitation, via a cascaded (deterministic + generative) framework on radar data for disaster management. For TRINETRA #1/#11: directly targets the extreme-rainfall tail that drives cloudbursts/flash-floods - the hardest, most safety-relevant regime; a benchmark + architectural idea (separate the mean field from the extreme/stochastic residual) relevant to how TRINETRA should forecast the triggering rainfall rather than smoothing away extremes.

title: Watch Your Step: Cost-Sensitive Accelerometer Fall Detection in Real-World Streaming
authors: Aderinola; Palmerini; D'Ascanio; Chiari; Klenk; Becker; Caulfield; Ifrim
relevance_component: cost-sensitive threshold tuning, miss>>FA, Recall 1.0
takeaway: Real-time streaming fall detection WITHOUT prior knowledge of events; introduces cost-sensitive learning that tunes the DECISION THRESHOLD using a cost function reflecting that missed falls are costlier than false alarms; achieves Recall 1.00 / Precision 0.84 / F1 0.91 on FARSEEING with <5ms inference. For TRINETRA #1/#9/#13: this is the DIRECT analogue of TRINETRA's miss-vs-FA tradeoff (Bayes p*=5/105) - a safety-critical streaming detector that tunes its threshold by an explicit asymmetric cost and still keeps FAs low; concrete evidence that cost-sensitive thresholding (not a fixed 0.5) is the right design, and that Recall 1.0 need not destroy precision. Strongly validates the alarm-threshold methodology and the #1 threshold-conflict fix.

title: CLAPS: Aleatoric-Epistemic Scaling via Last-Layer Laplace for Conformal Regression
relevance_component: conformal interval width adapts to aleatoric+epistemic
takeaway: Conformal regression gives marginal coverage but doesn't say how interval WIDTH should adapt across inputs; existing locally-adaptive methods capture only aleatoric noise, ignoring uncertainty from weak training support; CLAPS uses heteroscedastic last-layer Laplace uncertainty as the local normalization scale, combining input-dependent noise + epistemic uncertainty while keeping conformal validity; reduces to aleatoric scaling as epistemic contracts. For TRINETRA #13/#8: the calibrated people-at-risk interval should be WIDER where training support is thin (rare Himalayan extremes, new zones) - CLAPS is the principled way to make conformal intervals input-adaptive to BOTH noise types, fixing the #13 overclaim by widening honestly in the data-sparse tail rather than reporting uniform coverage.

title: Toward Robust Multimodal Learning using Multimodal Foundational Models (TRML)
relevance_component: generate virtual modality to replace missing one
takeaway: Real multimodal data is often INCOMPLETE; CLIP-style foundation models can't directly handle modality absence; TRML generates VIRTUAL modalities to replace missing ones and aligns their semantic space with the real ones via a missing-modality inference + semantic-matching module. For TRINETRA #10/#8/GMF: sensors drop out constantly (storm brownout #8, LoRa loss, cloud cover) - the fusion head must degrade gracefully when a modality is missing; TRML's generate-and-align pattern is one approach, but for a SAFETY system the key lesson is the failure mode exists and needs an explicit missing-modality strategy (reliability-gating candidate #10) rather than silent degradation.

title: Robust Multimodal Learning with Missing Modalities via Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
relevance_component: predict missing-modality embedding via prompt tuning
takeaway: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of unimodal pretrained models + self-supervised joint-embedding so the model PREDICTS the embedding of a missing modality at inference via prompt tuning, using available modalities; robust across varied missing-modality scenarios. For TRINETRA GMF/#10: a lightweight (parameter-efficient, edge-friendly) way to handle sensor dropout - impute the missing modality's representation rather than retrain; complements TRML (2401.13697) and informs the GMF per-modality reliability-gating design (candidate #10). Edge-efficiency matters given #14 compute budget.

title: Fully Heteroscedastic Count Regression with Deep Double Poisson Networks (DDPN)
relevance_component: input-conditional count uncertainty, over/under-dispersion
takeaway: Deep ensembles of Gaussian nets flexibly represent aleatoric uncertainty for CONTINUOUS regression but no analogue existed for COUNT regression; DDPN outputs Double-Poisson parameters enabling arbitrarily high/low predictive dispersion (over- and under-dispersion). For TRINETRA #8: 'people-at-risk' and event counts are COUNT quantities - modelling their uncertainty with a Gaussian is wrong; DDPN gives a calibrated count-uncertainty head so the risk estimate carries honest dispersion, improving the calibrated-people-at-risk module's statistical validity.

title: A deep-learning based Bayesian approach to seismic imaging and uncertainty quantification
relevance_component: SGLD + Bayesian model averaging for geophysical UQ
takeaway: Ill-conditioned geophysical inverse problems are nonunique; uses a randomly-initialized CNN as implicit structured prior, samples the posterior via stochastic-gradient Langevin dynamics, and performs BAYESIAN MODEL AVERAGING over samples; deep priors + BMA circumvent imaging artifacts, reduce overfitting under extreme noise, and yield pointwise variance (= uncertainty) that coincides with hard-to-image regions. For TRINETRA #8/#14: a template for principled UQ in a noisy geophysical setting via BMA (vs single-model); the idea that predictive variance flags where the model is unreliable maps onto flagging zones where TRINETRA's hazard estimate is least trustworthy (ties EVT/data-sparse tail).

title: Physics-informed neural networks for tsunami inundation modeling
relevance_component: PINN/DeepONet meshless shallow-water inundation
takeaway: Solves shallow-water equations for tsunami propagation + inundation with PINNs (meshless, simplifies inundation modelling); PINNs need retraining per initial condition, so they add DEEP OPERATOR NETS (DeepONet) that learn the solution OPERATOR for big speed-ups vs classical numerics; models both propagation and inundation well on classical benchmarks. For TRINETRA #11/#17: the flood/GLOF inundation + runout the physics gate needs is governed by shallow-water equations - a PINN/DeepONet surrogate could give fast on-device inundation estimates vs slow TRIGRS/hydrodynamic runs; the operator-net idea (train once, apply to many ICs) is key for real-time use. Also a caution: per-IC retraining is a known PINN limitation to design around.

title: Physics-informed neural networks for the shallow-water equations on the sphere
relevance_component: PINN SWE, multi-model for long horizons
takeaway: PINNs for shallow-water on the sphere (meteorological context); documents PINN TRAINING DIFFICULTIES over long time intervals and proposes a simple MULTI-MODEL approach (sequence of nets, one per sub-interval) plus encoding boundary conditions in a custom layer to avoid a BC loss. For TRINETRA #11/#17: concrete, honest engineering lessons for using PINNs on the hydrodynamics TRINETRA relies on - long-horizon PINNs are unstable and need temporal decomposition; informs whether a PINN surrogate is viable for multi-hour flood routing or whether classical solvers remain necessary.

title: Towards Digital Twin in Flood Forecasting with Data Assimilation of Satellite EO (Alzette)
authors: Nguyen; Bhattacharya; Wong; Didry; Phan; Tamisier; Matgen
relevance_component: particle-filter DA of Sentinel-1 into LISFLOOD-FP, 30-day
takeaway: Digital-Twin flood PoC assimilates Sentinel-1 flood-probability maps via a PARTICLE-FILTER data-assimilation process into a high-res LISFLOOD-FP hydrodynamic model + GloFAS products, giving daily forecasts up to 30 days with reduced uncertainty; honestly reports that GloFAS discharge-forecast uncertainty remains LARGE. For TRINETRA #1/#8/#11: this is the closest published analogue to TRINETRA's satellite-into-physics fusion - it shows (a) particle-filter DA of SAR into a hydraulic model works and improves over open-loop, and (b) the dominant residual uncertainty is in the upstream discharge forecast, exactly the kind of input-uncertainty TRINETRA must propagate rather than hide. Strong external benchmark + an honesty model for reporting residual uncertainty.

title: LLMs for Causal Relations Extraction in Social Media: Validation Framework for Disaster Intelligence
authors: Jeong; Vishnubhatla; Jiang; Harrison; Raglin; Liu
relevance_component: LLM causal graphs vs model priors - risk flagged
takeaway: Tests whether LLMs can extract causal relations from informal/fragmented disaster social-media posts; proposes an expert-grounded eval comparing LLM causal graphs to reference graphs from disaster reports AND assesses whether extracted relations are supported by post-event EVIDENCE or merely reflect MODEL PRIORS; highlights both potential and RISKS for decision-support. For TRINETRA #0/#13: if any LLM/agent is used in the decision-support or reporting layer, this is the cautionary evidence that LLM outputs may encode priors not evidence - demands a validation/grounding harness before trusting machine-generated situational causal claims; reinforces the #0 'don't trust unaudited automated success claims' lesson.

title: DisasterQA: A Benchmark for Assessing LLM Performance in Disaster Response
relevance_component: LLMs often confidently wrong on disaster advice
takeaway: Benchmark evaluating LLM disaster-response knowledge; central question is whether LLMs SHOULD be used for advice/decision-making in a disaster; finds accuracy/confidence issues that caution against uncritical reliance. For TRINETRA #0/#13: directly relevant if an LLM assists alerting/decisions - evidence that LLMs can be confidently wrong on exactly the high-stakes questions a warning system faces; argues for keeping LLMs out of the safety-critical decision path (or behind the conformal/shield gate) and for human-in-the-loop. Pairs with 2605.11348.

title: DUALFloodGNN: Physics-informed Graph Neural Network for Operational Flood Modeling
authors: Acosta; Herath; Lim; Saha; Rasnayaka; Marshall
relevance_component: physics-informed GNN, fast accurate flood hydrodynamics
takeaway: Physics-based flood models are accurate but too slow for operations; DUALFloodGNN embeds physical constraints at GLOBAL and LOCAL scales via explicit loss terms, jointly predicts node water-volume + edge flow in a shared message-passing net, trained with multi-step loss + dynamic curriculum for stable autoregressive inference; beats standard + SOTA GNN flood models on volume/flow/depth at high efficiency; open-sourced. For TRINETRA #11/#17: a current SOTA, fast, physics-INFORMED surrogate for the flood hydrodynamics the physics gate needs - directly usable to accelerate runout/inundation while keeping physical consistency; the global+local constraint design and curriculum for autoregressive stability are concrete engineering patterns, and open code/data make it a real benchmark.

title: StefaLand: An Efficient Geoscience Foundation Model Improving Dynamic Land-Surface Predictions
relevance_component: attribute-based geoscience FM, strong SPATIAL generalization
takeaway: StefaLand = generative spatiotemporal Earth representation model built to SUPPRESS overfitting via cross-domain interactions; location-aware masked autoencoder fusing static + time-series inputs, ATTRIBUTE-based (not image-based) representation that drastically cuts compute, residual fine-tuning adapters; strong SPATIAL generalization on 5 datasets / 4 tasks INCLUDING soil moisture and LANDSLIDES; trainable on ACADEMIC compute; beats SOTA supervised + fine-tuned vision FMs + commercial embeddings; explicitly aids DATA-POOR regions. For TRINETRA #2/#14/Kaggle-budget: this is arguably the single most on-point external FM - same tasks (landslide, soil moisture, streamflow), attacks the exact weaknesses (spatial generalization, concept drift, compute), and is Kaggle-feasible. A direct SOTA baseline/backbone candidate for the SSL encoder, and evidence the compute-heavy vision-FM path is NOT required.

title: Deep learning based landslide density estimation on SAR data for rapid response
authors: Boehm; Leong; Bal Mahesh; Prapas; Nemni; Kalaitzis; Ganju; Ramos-Pollan
relevance_component: SAR+elevation only landslide density, 0.814 AUC rapid
takeaway: Produces landslide DENSITY maps from Sentinel-1 SAR + elevation ONLY (no precipitation/soil-moisture/ancillary) for rapid emergency response after Hurricane Maria (USGS 71,431 landslide heads); 0.814 AUC at 128x128 chip level with just elevation + up to 3 pre/post SAR acquisitions; notes ~45% of landslides are smaller than a 10m Sentinel-1 pixel. For TRINETRA #1/#14/#18: honest benchmark of SAR-only landslide detection and its resolution LIMIT (sub-pixel landslides missed) - a crucial caveat for TRINETRA's Sentinel-1 reliance; also shows graceful degradation to minimal-input rapid-response mode when ancillary data is unavailable (relevant to sensor-dropout). Under-benchmarking (#18): a real baseline the report should cite.

title: Evaluating Opportunistic Routing Protocols in a Disaster Scenario (DTN Earthquake Case Study)
relevance_component: Epidemic vs Spray-and-Wait DTN, SnW better balance
takeaway: Evaluates DTN opportunistic routing in a realistic disaster (2016 Central Italy earthquake, stadium evacuation) with mobile+static nodes (crowd, responders, sensors, vehicles) in a PARTIALLY-CONNECTED environment; compares Epidemic vs Spray-and-Wait on delivery probability, latency, overhead, hop-count, drops; Spray-and-Wait gives best reliability/efficiency balance. For TRINETRA #8/#10: when LoRa/cellular backhaul is down (storm, remote valley), alerts must hop store-carry-forward; this is concrete evidence on WHICH DTN protocol to use (Spray-and-Wait over Epidemic) and the metrics to evaluate - directly informs the alert-dissemination resilience design the BOM/architecture currently omits.

title: HRSON: Home-based Routing for Smartphones in Opportunistic Networks
relevance_component: zero-knowledge DTN routing on non-ad-hoc smartphones
takeaway: Opportunistic (delay-tolerant) networks keep connectivity with limited infrastructure (e.g. natural disaster) via store-carry-forward; notes OS restrictions make ad-hoc mode infeasible on smartphones and that no common zero-knowledge routing exists for non-ad-hoc models; proposes HRSON for a self-organizing non-ad-hoc model. For TRINETRA #10: realistic constraint that consumer smartphones CAN'T do true ad-hoc DTN - any citizen-relayed alert dissemination must work within OS limits; informs feasibility of using the public's phones as DTN relays for last-mile warning delivery.

title: TinyissimoYOLO: Quantized Low-Memory TinyML Object Detection for Low-Power Microcontrollers
relevance_component: 422k-param INT8 YOLO, 180fps 196uJ on MAX78000
takeaway: Ultra-light quantized object detector: 422k params, <0.5MB weights, runs on MAX78000 CNN-accelerator MCU at up to 180fps and only 196uJ/inference (>106 MAC/cycle); 8-bit quantization-aware training deployed on STM32H7/L4, Apollo4b, MAX78000; practical limit ~3 classes due to size. For TRINETRA #9/#14/BOM: hard evidence that real-time visual detection CAN run on a milliwatt MCU - directly relevant to the River-Eye/CCTV edge node claims and the #14 edge-latency overclaim (shows what's actually achievable on an MCU vs the L40S-class GPU the report benchmarked on); the 3-class limit and 196uJ figure are concrete design/BOM numbers for a ₹2000 node.

title: Quantization and Deployment of Deep Neural Networks on Microcontrollers
relevance_component: int/float quantization framework for MCU deployment
takeaway: Studies embedding AI on low-power MCUs via quantization (fixed-point/int) and a deployment framework spanning common MCU targets; characterizes accuracy/memory/latency tradeoffs. For TRINETRA #9/#14/BOM: methodological backing for how to shrink the edge models (anomaly/VAD) to fit a ₹2000 MCU node - quantization is the lever; complements TinyissimoYOLO with the general recipe and the honest accuracy-vs-footprint tradeoff that the report must account for before claiming on-device inference.

title: Reducing False Ventricular Tachycardia Alarms in ICU Settings: A Machine Learning Approach
authors: Farayola; Akintola; Fagbohun; Oforgu; Kayode; Chimezie; Kadri; Oludotun; Ogbeide; Michael
relevance_component: ML false-alarm suppression, ROC-AUC>0.96, alarm fatigue
takeaway: Tackles ICU false-arrhythmia alarms that cause ALARM FATIGUE and compromise safety; uses the VTaC benchmark of annotated VT alarms, extracts time + frequency-domain waveform features, trains DL to classify TRUE vs FALSE alarms; ROC-AUC>0.96. For TRINETRA #1/#9/#13: a direct analogue of the system's core problem - a dedicated downstream classifier that SUPPRESSES false alarms (reducing cry-wolf fatigue, ties 2104.11422) without missing true events; evidence that a learned true/false-alarm discriminator over the primary detector is both feasible and high-AUC, supporting a two-stage alarm-verification layer in TRINETRA's pipeline. Validates investing in FA-reduction as a first-class component.

title: Sensor Drift Compensation via Olfactory System and Reservoir Computing
relevance_component: sample-wise ONLINE drift compensation, SNN+reservoir
takeaway: Addresses SENSOR DRIFT that degrades long-term reliability via gradual response shifts; conventional methods are batch; proposes true sample-wise ONLINE (no buffering) drift compensation using spiking neural nets (STDP feature adaptation) + spiking reservoir computing with winner-take-all self-supervised adaptation; handles gradual drift, random drift, SENSOR FAILURES, and abrupt changes. For TRINETRA #11/#14/candidate-#11: ground IoT sensors (tilt, soil-moisture, piezometers) drift and fail over months in the field - this is a label-free online-adaptation approach that distinguishes drift/failure patterns, directly relevant to the sensor-fault-vs-event discrimination risk (#11) and the concept-drift axis; a low-power spiking approach also suits edge nodes.

title: Estimating Wildfire Evacuation Decision and Departure Timing Using Large-Scale GPS Data
authors: Zhao; Xu; Lovreglio; Kuligowski; Nilsson; Cova; Wu; Yan
relevance_component: evacuation compliance ~46%, self/shadow evacuees dominate
takeaway: Uses large-scale GPS data to infer wildfire evacuation behaviour (2019 Kincade Fire); classifies self-evacuees, shadow evacuees, evacuees-under-warning, ordered-evacuees; finds self+shadow evacuees were >HALF of all evacuees, and total evacuation COMPLIANCE inside warning/order zones was only ~46%. For TRINETRA risk-candidate #8 / #13: HARD empirical number - under half of people in a warned zone actually comply, and a large share evacuate WITHOUT being told (shadow). This directly quantifies the evacuation-compliance/equity risk the people-at-risk and disruption-cost model must account for; a warning system optimizing lead time must model realistic ~46% compliance, not 100%. Critical input for the RL disruption-cost calibration and honest casualty estimates.

title: Identifying Trustworthiness Challenges in Deep Learning for Continental-Scale Water Quality Prediction
authors: Xia; Liu; Liu; Fang; Lu; Oymak; Currie; Liu
relevance_component: LSTM/DeepONet/Informer: spatial generalization to ungauged POOR
takeaway: Multi-dimensional trustworthiness benchmark of LSTM, DeepONet, Informer on 37yr / 482 US basins predicting 20 water-quality vars; finds systematic performance disparities by process complexity + data availability; management-critical variables least predictable/most uncertain; robustness tests show strong sensitivity to outliers/corrupted targets and the BEST-baseline model (LSTM) is MOST vulnerable under corruption; spatial generalization to UNGAUGED basins is poor across ALL models. For TRINETRA #14/#11/#18: direct evidence that (a) the strongest in-dist model can be the most fragile under data corruption (sensor faults!), and (b) spatial generalization to new/ungauged basins - exactly TRINETRA's deployment to new Himalayan catchments - is poor; demands cross-basin validation + robustness-to-corruption testing in the eval (#11 underpowered-eval, #14 OOD).

title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Short-Term Flood Prediction
relevance_component: Trend-Alignment physics loss on LSTM, data-scarce+extreme
takeaway: Pure data-driven LSTMs give physically inconsistent flood predictions and fail in data-scarce/extreme settings; proposes a PIML framework adding a Trend-Alignment constraint (penalizes directional inconsistency between precipitation and discharge trends) to the LSTM loss - no full hydrodynamic equations needed; raises NSE 0.20->0.23 at only 5% training data; under simulated extreme climate the baseline is UNSTABLE while the physics-informed model stays directionally consistent/plausible; honestly notes extreme PEAK magnitude still hard. For TRINETRA #11/#17/physics-gate: strong support for the physics-gate philosophy - a simple physical constraint stabilizes DL under extremes + data scarcity (both acute for Himalayan ungauged catchments); the honesty about residual peak-magnitude error is a model for TRINETRA's claims.

title: Deep Positive-Unlabeled Anomaly Detection for Contaminated Unlabeled Data
relevance_component: PU learning + deep SVDD/AE when unlabeled data is contaminated
takeaway: Semi-supervised anomaly detection usually assumes unlabeled data is mostly normal, but in practice it is CONTAMINATED with anomalies, weakening training; proposes deep positive-unlabeled anomaly detection integrating PU learning with autoencoders and DEEP SVDD, approximating normal-data anomaly scores from unlabeled + labeled-anomaly data WITHOUT labeled normal data; provides a generalization-error bound; beats baselines. For TRINETRA #8/Deep-SVDD-core: TRINETRA uses Deep SVDD in its anomaly ensemble and its 'normal' background is certainly contaminated by unlabeled real events; this is the principled fix (PU-aware Deep SVDD) with theory, directly hardening the anomaly-detection stage against the contaminated-normal assumption it currently makes implicitly.

title: OpenEarthMap: A Benchmark Dataset for Global High-Resolution Land Cover Mapping
relevance_component: 2.2M segments/97 regions/44 countries, UDA benchmark
takeaway: Global high-res land-cover benchmark: 2.2M segments from 5000 aerial/satellite images, 97 regions / 44 countries / 6 continents, 8-class labels at 0.25-0.5m GSD; models trained on it generalize worldwide; explicitly provides UNSUPERVISED DOMAIN ADAPTATION evaluation settings. For TRINETRA #2/#14/dataset-registry: a concrete, geographically-diverse EO benchmark + a ready UDA protocol to TEST cross-region generalization of the EO encoder - the exact capability TRINETRA needs to prove before deploying to new Himalayan regions; also a candidate pretraining/eval dataset for the registry. Addresses #18 under-benchmarking with a real public benchmark.

title: Bridging the Domain Gap in Satellite Pose Estimation: a Self-Training Approach
relevance_component: self-training UDA with geometric constraints, pseudo-labels
takeaway: Unsupervised domain adaptation for satellite pose estimation via self-training with domain-agnostic GEOMETRIC constraints; iterates pseudo-label generation + network training; won 1st on the sunlamp task of the 2nd Satellite Pose Estimation Competition. For TRINETRA #14: the SELF-TRAINING + domain-knowledge-constraint recipe (use physics/geometry to generate reliable pseudo-labels in the target domain) is transferable to adapting TRINETRA's detectors to a new region WITHOUT target labels - combine with the physics gate as the constraint source; a methodological template for label-free cross-region adaptation. Lower direct relevance (pose task) but the UDA-via-domain-constraint pattern is the useful transfer.

title: Evidential Deep Learning: Enhancing Predictive Uncertainty Estimation for Earth System Science
relevance_component: EDL = one-model aleatoric+epistemic UQ for geoscience
takeaway: Robust predictive UQ is critical for weather/climate; ensembles decompose uncertainty but are expensive; parametric DL estimates uncertainty with ONE model but misses epistemic; EVIDENTIAL deep learning estimates BOTH aleatoric + epistemic from a single deterministic model by predicting the parameters of a higher-order (evidential) distribution; applied to Earth-System-Science tasks. For TRINETRA #8/#13/#14: a cheap single-pass way to get decomposed uncertainty (crucial on an edge/compute budget #14) for the people-at-risk and hazard outputs - distinguishing 'noisy input' (aleatoric) from 'model out of its depth' (epistemic, = OOD/new-region flag); directly supports calibrated risk + abstention. Earth-science framing makes it a strong, domain-matched UQ baseline.

title: Uncertainty Estimation for Deep Reconstruction in Aquatic Disaster Scenarios with Autonomous Vehicles
authors: Yanes Luis; Casado Perez; Mendoza Barrionuevo; Diop; Toral Marin; Gutierrez Reina
relevance_component: EDL beats GP/MC-dropout/ensembles at UQ + lowest cost
takeaway: Compares Gaussian Processes, MC-Dropout, Deep Ensembles, and Evidential Deep Learning for scalar-field reconstruction + uncertainty decomposition from SPARSE sensor observations (aquatic monitoring, informative path planning); EDL gives best reconstruction accuracy AND best-calibrated uncertainty at the LOWEST inference cost; GPs limited by stationary-kernel assumption and intractable as density grows. For TRINETRA #8/#9/#14/sensor-placement: directly relevant to reconstructing hazard fields from TRINETRA's sparse ground sensors - head-to-head evidence that EDL is the cost-effective calibrated choice over GP/ensembles on an edge budget, and that epistemic uncertainty can drive WHERE to place/sample sensors (ties sensor-placement 2303.09750).

title: Gradient boosting with extreme-value theory for wildfire prediction
relevance_component: EVT-justified GB loss + SPATIAL cross-validation scheme
takeaway: Team Kohrrelation's EVA-2021-challenge approach to predicting wildfire COUNTS and SIZES over the US; uses EXTREME-VALUE-THEORY ideas in an ML context with theoretically-justified loss functions for gradient boosting, and devises a SPATIAL CROSS-VALIDATION scheme. For TRINETRA #11/#15/#1: two directly useful pieces - (1) EVT-grounded loss for rare extremes (reinforces 2310.03220/DI-GNN for TRINETRA's rare landslide/cloudburst tail) and (2) a concrete spatial-CV scheme, exactly the methodology needed to fix the #11 underpowered/leaky evaluation and avoid spatial autocorrelation leakage when validating across Himalayan catchments.

title: More Data or Better Algorithms: Latent Diffusion Augmentation for Deep Imbalanced Regression
relevance_component: LatentDiff synthesizes minority-region features for DIR
takeaway: Real regression data is heavily skewed; models learn majority samples and fail on MINORITY labels; deep imbalanced regression (DIR) lacked data-level solutions for high-dim inputs; proposes LatentDiff - conditional diffusion with priority-based generation to synthesize high-quality features in LATENT space for minority regions; efficient, modality-agnostic; improves minority regions while keeping overall accuracy. For TRINETRA #1/#11: hazard magnitude / people-at-risk / rainfall are HEAVILY imbalanced (rare large events = the minority region that matters most) - DIR methods target exactly the high-consequence tail the model currently underpredicts; latent augmentation is a concrete lever to improve rare-event regression without more real labels (which don't exist for Himalayan extremes).

title: Variational Imbalanced Regression: Fair Uncertainty Quantification via Probabilistic Smoothing
relevance_component: VIR: imbalanced regression + calibrated UQ via NIG
takeaway: Regression models underperform in BOTH accuracy and uncertainty when labels are imbalanced; VIR is a probabilistic DL model that borrows data with similar regression labels to compute a latent variational distribution, predicts normal-inverse-gamma distributions and modulates conjugate distributions for probabilistic reweighting; good imbalanced-regression accuracy + reasonable UQ as a byproduct. For TRINETRA #8/#1/#11: couples the two things TRINETRA needs together - accuracy on the rare-event tail AND calibrated uncertainty there (where it matters most); the NIG/evidential output pairs naturally with the evidential-DL direction (2309.13207) for the people-at-risk head.

title: p-DkNN: Out-of-Distribution Detection Through Statistical Testing of Deep Representations
authors: Dziedzic; Rabanser; Yaghini; Ale; Erdogdu; Papernot
relevance_component: p-values over hidden reps for OOD abstention, Neyman-Pearson
takeaway: Poorly-calibrated confidence makes NNs inadequate for safety-critical use; ability to ABSTAIN on OOD data is as important as classifying in-dist; p-DkNN analyzes similarity structure of intermediate hidden representations to compute p-VALUES for the end-to-end prediction - a statistically-founded uncertainty estimate; theory builds on Neyman-Pearson classification + selective classification (reject option); forces adaptive adversaries to make semantically meaningful changes. For TRINETRA #13/#14: a principled abstention/reject mechanism with statistical guarantees for the detector - abstain (defer to physics gate / human) when inputs are OOD (new region, novel storm), rather than emitting an overconfident alarm/non-alarm; complements conformal (#13) with a representation-level OOD test (#14).

title: Selective Probabilistic Classifier Based on Hypothesis Testing
relevance_component: reject option via Z-test on probabilistic net, low FPR
takeaway: Handles Closed-World-Assumption violation; prior reject methods threshold scores/loss but can't reach the LOW False-Positive-Ratio safety apps need; proposes a rejection option via HYPOTHESIS TESTING with probabilistic networks - estimates per-class outcome distributions and uses a Z-test on mean/std to reject uncertain outputs; achieves broader operating range + lower FPR than Softmax Response. For TRINETRA #13/#1: a reject-option mechanism tuned for LOW FPR - exactly the regime a landslide warning needs (keep false alarms down while abstaining on genuinely uncertain inputs); concrete alternative/complement to conformal + p-DkNN for the abstention layer.

title: Early Warning Index for Patient Deteriorations in Hospitals
authors: Bertsimas; Ma; Villalobos Carballo; Singh; Laskowski; Mather; Kombert; Haronian
relevance_component: human-in-loop multimodal EWS, SHAP, 3 risk tiers, deployed
takeaway: Multimodal ML Early Warning Index predicts aggregate risk (ICU admission, rapid-response dispatch, mortality) from structured+unstructured EHR; KEY design = HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP: clinicians help set alert THRESHOLDS and interpret outputs, enhanced by SHAP to show the drivers of each risk score; deployed as a dashboard stratifying patients into THREE risk tiers; C-statistic 0.796 on 18,633 patients; used as a live triage tool. For TRINETRA #13/risk-#8/warning-UX: a real deployed template for exactly TRINETRA's warning layer - human-set thresholds (not pure autonomy), explainable risk drivers, and a 3-tier stratification mirroring Green/Yellow/Orange/Red; evidence that keeping humans in the threshold/interpretation loop is the accepted safety-critical pattern, reinforcing the shield + human-in-loop stance over fully-autonomous alarms.

title: Riemannian Change Point Detection on Manifolds with Robust Centroid Estimation
relevance_component: streaming CPD, robust Huber vs Karcher centroid test stat
takeaway: Non-parametric change-point detection in STREAMING time series on Riemannian manifolds; monitors abrupt changes in the center of mass but avoids fragile step-size tuning by comparing a change-SENSITIVE Karcher mean vs a change-ROBUST Huber-function centroid (M-estimation), yielding a test statistic less sensitive to the estimation method; stochastic Riemannian optimization for efficiency. For TRINETRA #11/#14/candidate-#11: ground-sensor streams (tilt, SAR-derived covariance/coherence matrices are manifold-valued!) need online change detection that fires on real regime shifts but is ROBUST to drift/outliers - this robust-vs-sensitive centroid comparison is a principled streaming detector that could distinguish genuine pre-failure acceleration from sensor noise/drift, directly supporting the sensor-fault-vs-event discrimination.

title: Process Knowledge Driven Change Point Detection for Automated Model Calibration
relevance_component: PD-CPD fuses process knowledge into change detection
takeaway: Data-driven change-point methods assume changes are extraneous to the system and ignore available PROCESS KNOWLEDGE; proposes PD-CPD, a unified process-driven multivariate change-point framework combining CPD with ML and domain process models for automated calibration. For TRINETRA #11/#17/physics-gate: the philosophy mirrors TRINETRA's physics gate - fuse physical/process knowledge INTO the statistical change detector rather than treating signals as model-agnostic streams; supports a hybrid physics-informed change detector for triggering (e.g., couple Iverson/TRIGRS state with the anomaly detector) instead of a purely data-driven alarm.

title: FairHealth: Open-Source Python Library for Trustworthy Healthcare AI in Low-Resource Settings
relevance_component: fairness+explainability+equity toolkit for LMIC, disaster-aid module
takeaway: Open-source library for trustworthy ML in low-resource/LMIC settings (e.g. Bangladesh); modules for federated learning w/ homomorphic encryption, INTERSECTIONAL FAIRNESS metrics, fuzzy-SHAP explainability for LOW-BANDWIDTH decision support, multilingual triage, and EQUITABLE DISASTER-AID ALLOCATION; all public datasets, pip-installable. For TRINETRA risk-#8/#13: directly relevant to the equity dimension - a concrete toolkit pattern for fairness auditing + equitable resource/aid allocation + low-bandwidth explainability in exactly the Global-South, intermittent-connectivity context TRINETRA targets; supports building fairness/equity checks and low-bandwidth SHAP into the warning + aid-prioritization layer rather than treating all exposed populations as homogeneous.

title: Uncertainty Quantification With Multiple Sources
relevance_component: multi-source weighted conformal under covariate shift
takeaway: Weighted conformal prediction (WCP) handles covariate shift but relies on train/test covariate OVERLAP, which breaks in MULTI-SOURCE settings with varying covariate distributions; proposes two WCP extensions under a shared-conditional assumption: (i) merge-based aggregation of source-specific WCP sets and (ii) a data-pooling strategy jointly reweighting across sources; gives theoretical coverage guarantees. For TRINETRA #13/GMF/candidate-#10: TRINETRA fuses MULTIPLE heterogeneous sources (satellite, CCTV, LoRa ground nodes) each with its own distribution and shift - exactly the multi-source WCP problem; this is the principled way to get valid conformal intervals when per-modality covariate distributions differ, directly upgrading the per-zone Mondrian conformal to a multi-source-aware version and tying to GMF per-modality reliability gating.

title: Distribution-free risk assessment of regression-based machine learning algorithms
relevance_component: conformal failure-probability for regression intervals
takeaway: Targets the RISK-ASSESSMENT task: computing the probability that the true label lies within an interval around a regression model's prediction, critical for high-risk medicine/engineering; solves it with conformal prediction giving intervals guaranteed to contain the true label with a chosen probability. For TRINETRA #13/#1/people-at-risk: reframes conformal from 'interval width' to 'failure probability' - directly what a warning system needs ('what is the probability the true hazard/people-at-risk exceeds the alarm threshold?'); gives a distribution-free, honestly-calibrated statement of miss-risk for the regression outputs that feed the alarm policy, replacing the report's conformal overclaim (#13) with a defensible guarantee.

title: JMAC Protocol: A Cross-Layer Multi-Hop Protocol for LoRa
relevance_component: multi-hop LoRa mesh, predictive wake-up, long node lifetime
takeaway: LPWAN connectivity fails in non-line-of-sight / poor-coverage areas; JMAC is a cross-layer MULTI-HOP protocol for LoRa that exploits mesh behaviour to extend coverage and raise supported-device count per cell, using PREDICTIVE WAKE-UP for long sensor-node lifetime; validated in OMNeT++. For TRINETRA #6/#8/A10: directly addresses the Himalayan non-line-of-sight terrain problem - single-hop LoRa to a gateway will have coverage holes behind ridges; a multi-hop mesh with predictive wake-up both fills coverage AND preserves the battery budget the ₹2000 nodes need; concrete protocol evidence that the ground network should be mesh/multi-hop, not star, to survive terrain + the storm-brownout failure mode.

title: HaLert: A Resilient Smart City Architecture for Post-Disaster Based on Wi-Fi HaLow Mesh and SDN
relevance_component: post-disaster comms reuse via HaLow mesh + SDN
takeaway: Disasters are unpredictable, so reusing existing infrastructure for alternative post-disaster communication is essential to keep populations able to receive authority alerts; proposes HaLert, reusing dense distributed IoT via a Wi-Fi HaLow (sub-GHz, long-range) MESH + SDN control to stay resilient after a disaster. For TRINETRA #8/A10: the exact failure mode TRINETRA faces - the alarm must still reach people AFTER the triggering storm/landslide damages infrastructure; a self-healing sub-GHz mesh + software-defined rerouting is a design pattern for the 'last-mile alert survives the disaster' requirement, complementing the DTN/store-and-forward direction already in the notes for the comms-resilience workstream.

title: GLOFNet -- A Multimodal Dataset for GLOF Monitoring and Prediction
relevance_component: multimodal GLOF dataset: Sentinel-2 + ITS_LIVE + physical precursors
takeaway: GLOFs are rare but destructive; predictive research is hindered by FRAGMENTED, UNIMODAL data and most prior work only does POST-EVENT mapping; GLOFNet is a multimodal dataset focused on Shisper Glacier (Karakoram) integrating Sentinel-2 multispectral + NASA ITS_LIVE glacier-velocity products + physical precursors, harmonized for FORECASTING not just mapping. For TRINETRA #7/#15/dataset-registry: uses the SAME data sources TRINETRA names (Sentinel-2, ITS_LIVE) and tackles the exact rare-event/precursor-forecasting problem for GLOFs; a ready public multimodal benchmark for the GLOF pathway and a model for how to harmonize visual indicators with physical precursors - directly feeds the dataset registry (WS) and a cross-region GLOF eval; reinforces that forecasting (not mapping) is the hard, under-served regime.

title: Which Site, and When: A Free-Satellite-Data Test of Himalayan Glacial Lake Bursts, Landslides, and Ice Floods
relevance_component: CRITICAL reality-check: honest spatial-CV collapses AUC; DL does not beat GB
takeaway: Nearly a direct reality-check for TRINETRA's whole thesis. Uses the SAME free signals (InSAR moraine-dam deformation = WHICH lake; antecedent satellite weather = WHEN) for three hazards (moraine/ice-dam bursts, rainfall landslides, small glacier floods), each kept as two never-blended questions. 589 HMAGLOFDB dated outbursts + thousands of landslides, matched against similar-but-UNFAILED sites, under SPATIAL CROSS-VALIDATION that withholds WHOLE MAP TILES so no model wins by recognizing a trained neighbourhood. FINDINGS that hit TRINETRA hard: antecedent weather times the trigger at ROC 0.73 (big bursts)/0.83 (landslides)/0.82 (small floods); terrain susceptibility scored NAIVELY looks ~0.9 but HONESTLY (matched, spatial-CV) collapses to 0.76/0.71/0.54 (last = chance); FIVE deep-learning models DO NOT decisively beat a simple gradient-boosted baseline, and for lake hazards a THREE-RULE decision tree (ruggedness + monsoon rainfall) wins outright. For #11/#18/#1: hard external evidence that (a) naive spatial eval inflates AUC by ~0.15-0.35 (quantifies the #11 leakage bug), (b) DL over physics/GB is unjustified on free data (#18 under-benchmarking + novelty-vs-baseline), (c) honest achievable skill is modest - TRINETRA's performance claims must be re-stated under tile-withheld spatial-CV against a GB/decision-tree baseline or they are overclaims. This is the single most important external benchmark found.

title: Learning Safety Constraints from Demonstrations with Unknown Rewards
relevance_component: CoCoRL: convex safe set from safe demos, transferable constraints
takeaway: CoCoRL infers SHARED constraints in a CMDP from safe demonstrations with possibly DIFFERENT, UNKNOWN rewards and without known dynamics; builds a CONVEX safe set that provably guarantees safety even for sub-optimal-but-safe demos, converges to the true safe set with no regret for near-optimal demos, and the learned constraints TRANSFER across tasks/environments (IRL baselines learn unsafe policies). For TRINETRA #9/A6/shield: the shield constraints (FS<1->Orange, tilt>5deg/day->Red, etc.) are currently hand-set; CoCoRL offers a principled way to LEARN the safe-set from historical safe operations / expert evacuation decisions and transfer it across catchments - and the convex-safe-set formalism is exactly the realizability structure candidate-#2 (shield unrealizability) needs to avoid conflicting overrides.

title: Fuz-RL: A Fuzzy-Guided Robust Framework for Safe Reinforcement Learning under Uncertainty
relevance_component: fuzzy-measure-guided interpretable risk for safe RL under multi-source uncertainty
takeaway: Safe RL must perform well while staying safe, but multiple interacting uncertainty sources make interpretable risk assessment + robust decisions hard; Fuz-RL is a fuzzy-measure-guided robust framework for safe RL under uncertainty. For TRINETRA #9/A6/candidate-#13: TRINETRA's alarm policy faces exactly multi-source uncertainty (sensor noise, forecast error, model epistemic); a fuzzy-measure approach to interpretable risk aligns with the need for an explainable, uncertainty-aware safe policy rather than a brittle fixed-threshold shield - complements the evidential-UQ direction for the decision layer.

title: Beyond Backscatter: AlphaEarth Land-Cover Priors for Rapid SAR Flood Segmentation Across Foundation Backbones
relevance_component: single-temporal SAR flood ambiguity; land-context priors; per-event eval mandatory
takeaway: Rapid flood mapping: optical often unusable during floods, and SINGLE-TEMPORAL SAR is AMBIGUOUS - new inundation, permanent water, and other smooth surfaces give similar backscatter. Tests whether stable land-context priors help post-event SAR flood seg when no registered seasonally-matched pre-event image exists; compares 4 backbones (scratch UNet, ImageNet-UNet, SAR-pretrained TerraMind ViT, optical-pretrained DINOv3 ViT) in SAR-only / SAR+DEM / SAR+AlphaEarth under identical fusion+split; evaluated on held-out Hurricane Florence + Louisiana. Both auxiliary priors beat SAR-only; AlphaEarth best on harder Florence, DEM best/more-stable on Louisiana; CROSS-EVENT performance tracks flood-class prevalence + similarity to training distribution -> explicitly 'underscoring the need for PER-EVENT evaluation'. For TRINETRA #11/#8/flood-pathway: (a) confirms single-temporal SAR flood detection is physically ambiguous (TRINETRA's River-Eye/SAR flood signal needs bi-temporal or land-priors), (b) independent corroboration that per-event (not pooled) evaluation is mandatory, echoing 2608.12422; (c) DEM + land-cover priors are cheap, available auxiliaries to disambiguate inundation.

title: Improved Flood Insights: Diffusion-Based SAR to EO Image Translation
relevance_component: diffusion SAR->EO translation for flood interpretability
takeaway: Proposes a diffusion-based SAR->EO (optical) image translation to make SAR flood observations more human-interpretable, since SAR is hard to read and optical is cloud-blocked during floods. For TRINETRA flood-pathway/warning-UX: a route to present SAR-derived flood extent as interpretable optical-like imagery for responder/operator dashboards (ties to human-in-loop #13), and a data-augmentation idea for cloud-blocked periods; secondary relevance but a real tool for the operator-facing layer.

title: Bi-temporal SAR flood detection network (Sen1Floods11)
relevance_component: bi-temporal SAR beats uni-temporal flood detection by 6% IoU
takeaway: A bi-temporal SAR flood-detection network evaluated on Sen1Floods11; combining PRE+POST event SAR with an effective architecture beats the uni-temporal SOTA by 6% IoU. NOTE: arXiv number was in the pruned feed middle so is NOT recorded (no guessing); the DOI 10.1109/IGARSS46834.2022.9883132 is fully visible and authoritative. For TRINETRA #11/flood: quantifies that BI-TEMPORAL (change-based) SAR is materially better than single-image flood detection (+6% IoU), reinforcing 2606.29134 - TRINETRA should use pre/post change rather than single-pass SAR for inundation.

title: Avalanche Prediction and Dynamics using Temperature Variance Grain Size Variance and Flow Regimes
relevance_component: SVM avalanche forecasting from met+snowpack; MPM flow regimes
takeaway: Combines Material Point Method (MPM) modelling of snow-avalanche flow regimes with SVM forecasting using meteorological + snowpack variables (snowfall, accumulation, rain interaction, snowdrift, snowpack mechanics, temperature profile); notes MPM captured flow patterns but struggled with powder clouds. For TRINETRA (avalanche is an in-scope Himalayan hazard not deeply covered in BOM/physics): identifies the concrete feature set for snow-avalanche triggering and shows a physics(MPM)+ML(SVM) hybrid - relevant if TRINETRA extends to snow avalanches, and a reminder that the current physics stack (Iverson/TRIGRS for rain-triggered slides) does NOT cover snow-avalanche mechanics; a scope-coverage gap to flag.

title: Statistical models for short and long term forecasts of snow depth
relevance_component: zero-inflated gamma regression for snow depth forecasting
takeaway: Statistical snow-depth forecast models: short-term (given reliable temp+precip forecasts) with covariates entered NONLINEARLY following snowfall/aging/melting physics, and because many observations are zero snow depth, uses a ZERO-INFLATED GAMMA regression (as in precipitation modelling); also long-term forecasts. For TRINETRA #1/rare-event-modelling: the zero-inflated structure is exactly the statistical shape of hazard-trigger data (mostly zero/no-event, occasional large positive) - a principled template for modelling the many-zeros-plus-heavy-tail distribution of rainfall/trigger intensity, complementing the deep-imbalanced-regression papers (2306.06599/2509.23240) with a simple, calibrated parametric baseline that TRINETRA's eval should include.

title: Rethinking deep learning: linear regression remains a key benchmark in predicting terrestrial water storage
authors: Nie; Kumar; Chen; Zhao; Skulovich; Yoo; Pflug; Ahmad; Konapala
relevance_component: LINEAR REGRESSION beats LSTM + Temporal-Fusion-Transformer for TWS
takeaway: Using the open global HydroGlobe dataset (baseline from a land-surface model + an advanced version with multi-source remote-sensing data assimilation), shows LINEAR REGRESSION is a robust benchmark that OUTPERFORMS the more complex LSTM and Temporal Fusion Transformer for terrestrial-water-storage prediction; stresses including traditional statistical models as benchmarks and building globally-representative benchmark datasets. For TRINETRA #18/#11: a SECOND independent 'simple baseline beats deep model' result (with 2608.12422) in exactly the geoscience-hydrology domain - TRINETRA MUST benchmark its deep stack against linear/GB baselines on the same data or its complexity is unjustified; also validates the data-assimilation input path and warns that natural-variability + human-modification make land-surface states hard, so claimed skill must be shown over a trivial benchmark.

title: Prolongation of SMAP to Spatio-temporally Seamless Coverage of Continental US Using a Deep Learning Neural Network
relevance_component: first LSTM in hydrology; gap-fills SMAP soil moisture, robust spatial extrapolation
takeaway: First application of LSTM in hydrology: predicts SMAP L3 surface soil moisture from atmospheric forcing + model-simulated moisture + static physiographic attributes, removing most model bias and achieving RMSE<0.035, correlation>0.87 over 75% of CONUS incl. forested Southeast; explicitly ROBUST for temporal AND spatial extrapolation and generalizes across climates - with high fidelity to SMAP, good for hindcasting + DATA ASSIMILATION. For TRINETRA SMAP-input/#8: TRINETRA uses SMAP (short span, irregular revisit) - this is the canonical method to gap-fill SMAP into a seamless soil-moisture field (a key landslide predisposing variable) and evidence that LSTM soil-moisture CAN spatially extrapolate (nuance vs the 'DL fails spatial-CV' results: works for soil-moisture regression, fails for rare-event hazard classification - the distinction matters for which pipeline stage uses DL).

title: Offline RL Without Off-Policy Evaluation
relevance_component: ONE-STEP policy improvement beats iterative OPE-based offline RL; OPE is high-variance
takeaway: Shows that a SINGLE step of constrained/regularized policy improvement using an on-policy Q-estimate of the BEHAVIOR policy performs surprisingly well - beating iterative actor-critic (OPE-based) methods on much of D4RL, while being simpler and far more robust to hyperparameters; argues iterative approaches suffer from the HIGH VARIANCE inherent in repeated off-policy evaluation. For TRINETRA #9/A5/RL-design: TRINETRA's 4-stage RL plans iterative offline RL (CQL/IQL) then PPO; this is strong evidence that (a) a simpler one-step offline-RL baseline should be tried first and may win, (b) iterative OPE compounds variance - directly relevant to the brittle-reward concern (#9) and to honest RL evaluation; argues for simpler, more robust alarm-policy learning before heavy machinery.
