title: Hybrid Value Estimation for Off-policy Evaluation and Offline Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: HVE trades bias/variance between offline-data and model value estimates; better error bound
takeaway: Hybrid Value Estimation (HVE) reduces value-estimation error by trading off bias and variance - balancing value estimates from offline DATA vs a learned MODEL; proves a better error bound than direct methods; instantiated as OPHVE (off-policy evaluation) and MOHVE (model-based offline RL), validated on MuJoCo. For TRINETRA #9/A5: offers the principled OPE machinery TRINETRA needs to HONESTLY estimate the value of a candidate alarm policy from historical data before deployment (and to pick among CQL/IQL/one-step), with explicit bias-variance control - exactly the off-policy-evaluation rigour the alarm-policy stage currently lacks; pairs with 2106.08909's caution that naive iterative OPE is high-variance.

title: TinyissimoYOLO: A Quantized, Low-Memory Footprint, TinyML Object Detection Network for Low Power Microcontrollers
relevance_component: 422k-param 8-bit YOLO on MCU: 180fps, 196uJ/inference, <0.5MB
takeaway: Ultra-lightweight quantized object-detection CNN (422k params, <0.5MB weights) running real-time on milliwatt microcontrollers; on MAX78000 CNN-accelerator reaches up to 180fps at only 196uJ/inference (>106 MAC/cycle); 8-bit quantization-aware training, deployed on STM32H7A3/L4R9/Apollo4b/MAX78000; but with such a small net, only up to 3 object-detection classes are practical. For TRINETRA #14/candidate-#12/A9 (edge VAD): a concrete reality-check on what object detection on a cheap low-power MCU can actually do - tiny multi-class detection at high fps IS feasible on a hardware CNN accelerator, BUT limited to ~3 classes and sub-0.5MB models; this bounds the River-Eye/CCTV edge node design and confirms the Cerberus-on-L40S VAD (#14) cannot run on an MCU - either use an accelerator-class edge SoC or restrict the edge model to a tiny detector + backhaul for the heavy stack. Directly supports the tiered edge->cloud mandate.

title: BACON: A fully explainable AI model with graded logic for decision making problems
relevance_component: fully-explainable, human-tunable graded-logic decision model
takeaway: Argues that high-stakes autonomous decisions (healthcare/security/finance/robotics) need models that are not only accurate but FULLY EXPLAINABLE and HUMAN-TUNABLE for end-to-end transparency; introduces BACON, a graded-logic decision model. For TRINETRA #13/candidate-#13/shield: the shield + alarm rule layer should be exactly this - a transparent, human-tunable decision structure rather than an opaque learned policy; graded logic (soft AND/OR over hazard criteria) is a candidate formalism for combining FS, tilt-rate, rainfall, GLOF signatures into an explainable escalation decision that operators can inspect and tune, aligning with the human-in-loop finding (2512.14683). NOTE: the broader 'explainable high-stakes' arXiv space (219 hits) was dominated by LLM reasoning/fact-verification papers (DecisionFlow, ArgRAG) judged OUT OF SCOPE for TRINETRA - not logged, to avoid padding.

title: Integrating Newton's Laws with deep learning for enhanced physics-informed compound flood modelling
relevance_component: ALPINE PINN: FULL shallow-water (mass+both momentum) compound-flood emulator; physics helps MOST at peak
takeaway: ALPINE (All-in-one Physics-Informed Neural Emulator) enforces COMPLETE shallow-water dynamics (mass conservation + BOTH momentum equations, not partial constraints) for COMPOUND floods (surge+tide+rainfall+river discharge interacting); ConvEncoder-Decoder + ConvLSTM, composite data+physics-residual loss; 6 storms (4 train/1 val/1 held-out), substantial gains over plain NN; crucially 'physics-informed constraints prove MOST valuable during PEAK STORM INTENSITY when multiple drivers interact and reliable predictions matter most'. For TRINETRA physics-gate/#4/flash-flood: strong external validation that enforcing full physics (vs partial/none) buys the most accuracy exactly in the extreme regime TRINETRA cares about - supports keeping a hard physics gate over pure-DL; and ALPINE is a fast physically-consistent flood emulator usable for TRINETRA's flood pathway + ensemble risk analysis; compound (multi-driver) framing matches Himalayan cloudburst+river scenarios.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Two-Dimensional Shallow Water Equations with Terrain Topography and Rainfall Source Terms
relevance_component: 2D shallow-water PINN with terrain + rainfall source terms
takeaway: PINN solving the 2D shallow-water equations WITH terrain topography and RAINFALL source terms - i.e. rainfall-driven overland/flash flooding on real terrain. For TRINETRA flash-flood/cloudburst pathway/#4: directly the governing-equation setup for rainfall-triggered flash floods on Himalayan terrain; a mesh-free emulator that ingests rainfall as a source term and respects topography is a candidate for the flood-routing component and for cross-checking the physics gate's hydrology; complements ALPINE (coastal compound) with the inland rainfall-on-terrain case TRINETRA actually faces.

title: Neural Ensemble Search for Uncertainty Estimation and Dataset Shift
authors: Zaidi; Zela; Elsken; Holmes; Hutter; Teh
relevance_component: VARYING-architecture ensembles beat deep-ensembles on calibration + dataset shift
takeaway: Deep ensembles (SOTA UQ) only ensemble random inits of a FIXED architecture; proposes building ensembles with VARYING architectures, exploiting architectural variation as a diversity source; the resulting ensembles beat deep ensembles on accuracy, uncertainty CALIBRATION, and robustness to DATASET SHIFT - and can win even with weaker average base learners because of higher diversity. For TRINETRA GMF/#13/candidate-#10/#14: TRINETRA's meta-fusion fuses several experts (physics base + anomaly members + forecasters); this says DIVERSITY of expert architecture materially improves calibrated UQ and shift-robustness - argues for deliberately heterogeneous experts in GMF (not clones) and gives a principled reason the stacked head should preserve diverse base learners; directly supports better-calibrated people-at-risk under distribution shift (new catchments/seasons).

title: What, Where and How to Transfer in SAR Target Recognition Based on Deep CNNs
relevance_component: ImageNet pretraining transfers POORLY to SAR; optical->SAR discrepancy; transitive multi-source DA
takeaway: SAR interpretation lacks labeled data; the prevalent fix (fine-tune an ImageNet-pretrained model) performs POORLY for SAR because of the prominent discrepancy between SAR and optical images; studies what/where/how to transfer, proposes a TRANSITIVE transfer via multi-source data with domain adaptation to shrink source-SAR discrepancy (OpenSARShip). Key: 'universal conclusions about transfer learning in natural images CANNOT be completely applied to SAR targets.' For TRINETRA #18/#2/A2: TRINETRA leans on EO foundation models + SSL - but most FMs are optical/ImageNet-lineage; this warns that optical-pretrained features transfer poorly to Sentinel-1 SAR (TRINETRA's core InSAR modality), so a frozen optical EO-FM baseline may underperform on the SAR branch and SAR-specific pretraining / domain adaptation is needed; sharpens the encoder-design + benchmarking argument.

title: FlowEO: Generative Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Earth Observation
relevance_component: generative unsupervised domain adaptation for EO
takeaway: FlowEO: a generative UNSUPERVISED domain-adaptation approach for Earth-observation imagery (adapting a model to a new unlabeled target domain). For TRINETRA #18/A14/cross-region: deploying TRINETRA in a new catchment/sensor/season is an unsupervised domain shift with NO new labels - generative UDA is a candidate to adapt the EO encoder/segmenter to new Himalayan regions without labeled landslide data there, directly addressing the spatial-generalization failure quantified by 2608.12422; a method lead for the drift/OOD adaptation workstream.

title: Dual Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Sound Event Detection
relevance_component: dual KD compresses sound-event-detection to 1/3 params for edge, beats baseline
takeaway: Dual knowledge distillation for on-device Sound Event Detection: temporal-averaging KD (mean-student from temporal averaging of student params, for STABLE distillation) + embedding-enhanced feature distillation (embedding layer for contextual learning); on DCASE2023 Task4A, a student with only ONE-THIRD the baseline params BEATS it on PSDS1/PSDS2 - ideal for edge devices. For TRINETRA A9/#14/candidate-#12 (edge acoustic): TRINETRA could use acoustic/infrasound signatures (debris-flow roar, GLOF) at edge nodes; this shows a compact SED model can run on-device with strong detection at 1/3 size - a concrete recipe to put event detection on cheap field nodes while a heavier teacher trains offline; supports the tiered edge->cloud design and the ₹2000 node compute envelope.

title: Energy-Efficient Plant Monitoring via Knowledge Distillation
relevance_component: distill heavy ViT/FM teacher into compact low-energy student for field monitoring
takeaway: SOTA plant species/disease recognition uses high-capacity ViTs / multimodal FOUNDATION MODELS that are too computationally heavy for field deployment; uses knowledge distillation to compress into an energy-efficient student for on-device environmental monitoring. For TRINETRA #14/candidate-#12/A9: the exact pattern TRINETRA needs for its CCTV/River-Eye edge nodes - the heavy encoder/VAD (Cerberus-class, L40S) is the TEACHER, trained offline; a distilled compact student runs at the edge within the ₹2000 power/compute budget; direct evidence this teacher->student compression is viable for energy-constrained environmental field monitoring, operationalizing the tiered design that resolves the edge-latency/compute bug (#14).

title: Graph Neural Network-based surrogate model for granular flows
relevance_component: GNN surrogate learns granular-flow (landslide/debris-flow) dynamics, fast forward model
takeaway: GNN surrogate for granular-flow dynamics (landslides, debris flows), modelling the dynamic particle rearrangement and complex solid<->fluid-like transitions; learns next-step evolution from current graph state, giving a fast differentiable forward simulator vs expensive high-fidelity solvers. For TRINETRA #11/A11/runout: a fast GNN runout/dynamics emulator could replace or augment the Scheidegger/Froehlich empirical runout in TRINETRA for debris-flow reach + impact estimation, enabling many scenarios cheaply for people-at-risk under different triggers; pairs with its companion differentiable-GNS inverse paper (2401.13695, already a dedup marker) - together they are the fast-forward + inverse pair for granular-flow risk, a concrete upgrade path for the runout component.

title: Spatial Modeling and Risk Zoning of Global Extreme Precipitation via Graph Neural Networks and r-Pareto Processes
relevance_component: GNN + r-Pareto EVT risk-zoning on IMERG; nonstationary spatial tail dependence
takeaway: Hybrid GNN + r-Pareto-process (GNN-rP) framework for spatial EXTREME-precipitation modelling + risk zoning; learns nonlinear NONSTATIONARY dependence from precipitation-derived spatial graphs and applies a data-driven TAIL functional for joint exceedances in a low-dim embedding; uses NASA IMERG (2000-2021) + CMIP6 SSP5-8.5; delineates coherent high-risk zones, quantifies temporal persistence, detects emerging hotspots; beats 2 baselines on pointwise high-risk-cell detection; notes extreme precip triggers COMPOUND flooding + landslides. For TRINETRA #1/#3/A3: directly uses TRINETRA's GPM-IMERG input and couples ML with EXTREME VALUE THEORY for the heavy rainfall tail that drives the I-D thresholds (#15) and physics gate - a principled spatial-extremes method for nonstationary monsoon precipitation, and a template for honest tail modelling + risk zoning rather than fixed thresholds; recovered ID via author search (not guessed).

title: Routing-Free Mixture-of-Experts
relevance_component: eliminates centralized router/Softmax/TopK/load-balancing; experts self-activate
takeaway: Standard MoE relies on CENTRALIZED routing that injects rigid inductive biases; Routing-Free MoE removes external routers, Softmax, Top-K and load balancing, instead encapsulating activation inside each expert via continuous gradient flow so each expert decides its own activation; adds a unified adaptive load-balancing framework interpolating expert- and token-balancing; reports better scalability + ROBUSTNESS vs baselines. For TRINETRA GMF/candidate-#3/#10: TRINETRA's Gated Meta-Fusion uses a gated MoE head; this is direct evidence that centralized Top-K routing is brittle and that a routing-free / self-gating design is more robust - relevant to the GMF multicollinearity/instability risk (candidate #3) and to the per-modality reliability-gating idea (candidate #10, where each expert's self-activation can encode its own reliability); a concrete alternative to a fragile learned router over correlated experts.

title: An Efficient Unsupervised Federated Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Heterogeneous IoT Networks
relevance_component: unsupervised FL anomaly detection for HETEROGENEOUS IoT, no raw-data transmission
takeaway: Federated learning for IoT keeps diverse-device data LOCAL while contributing to a shared global model, inherently preserving privacy and avoiding raw-data transmission; tackles the HETEROGENEITY of IoT data (device capability, format, comms-constraint differences) with an efficient UNSUPERVISED anomaly-detection approach. For TRINETRA #8/#11/A10: TRINETRA's ground IoT + River-Eye nodes are exactly heterogeneous, largely UNLABELED, and bandwidth-starved over LoRa; FL lets each node learn/adapt a local anomaly model and share only model updates (fits the storm-brownout + narrow-LoRa constraint of #8), and unsupervised operation matches the no-labels reality - a concrete architecture for distributed, privacy-preserving, bandwidth-light anomaly detection across the sensor field, and a partial mitigation for sensor-fault-vs-event (candidate #11) via cross-node model consistency.

title: FedIoT: Federated Learning for Internet of Things
authors: Zhang; He; Ma; Gao; Ma; Avestimehr
relevance_component: federated anomaly detection benchmark for resource-constrained IoT; affordable on-device
takeaway: Federated-learning framework/benchmark (FedIoT) for anomaly detection on resource-constrained IoT devices, shown affordable and promising for on-device training; open source (FedML-AI/FedIoT). NOTE: arXiv number was in the pruned feed middle so NOT recorded (no guessing); DOI 10.1145/3485730.3493444 is fully visible and authoritative. For TRINETRA #8/A10: an established, benchmarked FL-for-IoT baseline demonstrating that federated anomaly detection is feasible within tight device budgets - evidence base for the distributed-learning option on TRINETRA's ₹2000 nodes; pairs with 2602.24209 (heterogeneous/unsupervised) as the practical reference implementation.

title: Hierarchical Selective Classification
relevance_component: abstain by COARSENING prediction under uncertainty; hierarchical risk-coverage guarantee
takeaway: Extends selective classification to a HIERARCHICAL setting: instead of a binary predict/reject, the model REDUCES SPECIFICITY under uncertainty (backs off to a coarser class), using the class hierarchy; formalizes hierarchical risk+coverage, gives inference rules and an algorithm that guarantees a target accuracy with high probability. For TRINETRA #13/candidate-#13/alarm-levels: TRINETRA's alarm has an ORDINAL hierarchy (Green<Yellow<Orange<Red); this is the natural formalism to abstain by issuing a COARSER/lower-confidence alert (e.g. 'elevated watch' instead of a specific Red) when uncertain, with a provable risk-coverage guarantee - directly operationalizes a principled, calibrated escalation that degrades gracefully rather than mis-firing a specific level; pairs with the conformal + reject-option machinery already in the synthesis.

title: Confidence-aware Contrastive Learning for Selective Classification
relevance_component: generalization bound shows FEATURE-level optimization improves selective classification; CCL-SC
takeaway: Provides a GENERALIZATION BOUND for selective classification showing that optimizing FEATURE layers (not just the classification head) improves selective performance; proposes CCL-SC (confidence-aware contrastive learning) that similarizes features of homogeneous instances and differentiates heterogeneous ones, strength controlled by model confidence. For TRINETRA #13/candidate-#4 (Deep-SVDD): the theory that selective-prediction quality is driven at the FEATURE/representation level is directly relevant to TRINETRA's SSL encoder + Deep-SVDD anomaly core - a well-shaped feature space improves both abstention and anomaly separation; argues the encoder (not just the decision head) should be trained with abstention/confidence awareness.

title: Measurement Optimization under Uncertainty using Deep Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: RL agent places heterogeneous sensors to maximize info gain under uncertainty
takeaway: Casts optimal sensor placement under system/parameter UNCERTAINTY as an MDP; a DRL agent places a budgeted number of HETEROGENEOUS sensor types to maximize an INFORMATION-THEORETIC reward (info gain), handling uncertainties that make deterministic placement insufficient; demonstrated on a shear-building model. For TRINETRA deployment/WS (IoT siting)/#8/A10: TRINETRA must decide WHERE to put a limited budget of ₹2000 LoRa/River-Eye nodes across 110,000 km2 for maximum early-warning value - this is exactly a budgeted, heterogeneous, uncertainty-aware info-gain placement problem; a concrete method for the node-siting workstream (complements the GP/mutual-information placement paper 2303.00028 already in ledger), and ties placement to the people-at-risk objective rather than ad-hoc siting.

title: Impact of Human Behavior on Social Opportunistic Forwarding
relevance_component: DTN opportunistic forwarding under long delays/partitions; human-mobility-driven delivery
takeaway: Delay-tolerant networking via OPPORTUNISTIC message forwarding for environments with very long delays + frequent network PARTITIONS (disaster areas, development regions), with limited end-to-end connectivity + node resources; studies how human mobility/behaviour drives forwarding-algorithm performance. For TRINETRA #8/A10: after a landslide/flood severs infrastructure, alerts + sensor data must still propagate via store-carry-forward over intermittent links; this quantifies that delivery depends on human/courier mobility patterns - informs a DTN fallback layer for last-mile warning dissemination when LoRa/cellular backhaul is down (the storm-brownout failure of #8), and warns that opportunistic delivery latency is mobility-dependent, so critical Red alerts need a guaranteed path (satellite backhaul) not just opportunistic relay.

title: WATCH: Wasserstein Change Point Detection for High-Dimensional Time Series Data
relevance_component: unsupervised Wasserstein CPD for high-dim unlabeled streams
takeaway: WATCH: Wasserstein-distance change-point detection that models an initial distribution and monitors its drift as new points arrive, giving accurate robust UNSUPERVISED detection in high-dimensional UNLABELED streams (where most CPD methods fail); beats SOTA on many benchmarks. For TRINETRA #11/candidate-#5/candidate-#11/A14: TRINETRA's sensor fabric is a high-dim unlabeled stream subject to (a) regime shifts (season/climate - endogenous feedback candidate #5), (b) sensor drift/faults (candidate #11). An unsupervised distributional CPD is the right trigger to (i) flag when the deployed model's input distribution has shifted enough to warrant recalibration/conformal reset, (ii) distinguish a slow distributional drift from an abrupt real-event spike - a concrete monitoring primitive for the drift/OOD workstream.

title: Beyond Euclidean Summaries: Online Change Point Detection for Distribution-Valued Data
relevance_component: online CPD on distribution/shape geometry, not moment summaries
takeaway: Argues existing online CPD relies on fixed-dim Euclidean (moment/feature) summaries that OBSCURE changes in distributional SHAPE/geometry; proposes an intrinsic distribution-valued online CPD, and contributes challenging multi-entity multivariate CPD datasets. For TRINETRA #11/candidate-#5/A14: some hazard precursors manifest as a change in the SHAPE of a sensor's distribution (e.g. tilt-rate variance/skew increasing before failure) not just its mean - a shape-aware online CPD could catch precursory regime changes that moment-based monitors miss; complements WATCH as a more sensitive (if heavier) drift/precursor detector; also a reminder to monitor higher-order distributional features of the sensor streams, not just means/thresholds.

title: Modeling of unsaturated flow through porous media using meshless methods
relevance_component: meshless RBF + Kirchhoff + Picard for Richards eqn infiltration
takeaway: Solves the RICHARDS equation (unsaturated water flow in soils) with a MESHLESS localized radial-basis-function method + Kirchhoff transformation, Picard iterations for the nonlinearity; the difficulty is the nonlinear unsaturated hydraulic conductivity + capillary-pressure function; validated vs Hydrus in 1D/2D for sandy-clay/loam. For TRINETRA #2/#3/#17/A4 (physics gate): TRINETRA's rainfall-infiltration -> pore-pressure path (feeding Iverson transient psi and the FS computation) IS the Richards equation; this gives an efficient infiltration solver and, importantly, documents the NUMERICAL difficulty (strong nonlinearity) that TRINETRA's simplified Iverson analytic form papers over - supports the finding that the transient-pressure modelling is a soft spot and that infiltration should be solved/validated properly (vs Hydrus) rather than assumed; van-Genuchten/Kirchhoff machinery named for the fix.

title: A study on iterative methods for solving Richards' equation
relevance_component: linearization/iterative schemes (Newton/Picard/L-scheme) for degenerate Richards eqn
takeaway: Studies LINEARIZATION methods (backward-Euler in time, Galerkin FE in space) for efficiently solving the Richards equation - a DEGENERATE elliptic-parabolic equation for saturated/unsaturated porous-media flow; compares iterative schemes (e.g. Newton vs Picard vs L-scheme type) for the nonlinear system. For TRINETRA #2/#3/#17/A4: establishes that solving the pore-pressure/infiltration physics TRINETRA relies on is numerically delicate (degenerate nonlinearity, convergence of the linearization matters) - reinforces that the analytic Iverson shortcut has limits and that a robust iterative Richards solver is the principled backbone for the physics gate's transient suction/FS terms; names the standard linearization toolkit for a correct implementation.

title: End-to-End Intelligent Framework for Rockfall Detection
authors: Zoumpekas; Puig; Salamo; Garcia-Selles; Blanco Nunez; Guinau
relevance_component: ML pipeline detects rockfall clusters in TLS point clouds; EXTREME imbalance needs heavy resampling
takeaway: End-to-end ML framework to detect rockfall events in Terrestrial-Laser-Scanner point clouds (replacing tedious manual multi-temporal visual comparison); because rockfall is EXTREMELY imbalanced, it benchmarks many resampling techniques + models + feature-selection pipelines; validated on two Spanish cliffs (basaltic + conglomerate). For TRINETRA SCOPE-GAP/#11/A11: rockfall is a distinct Himalayan road/settlement hazard that TRINETRA's Iverson/TRIGRS infinite-slope + hydrology stack does NOT model (it is a discrete rigid-block detachment, not a saturated slope failure) - a coverage gap worth flagging; methodologically it reconfirms the #11 lesson that rare-event geohazard detection lives or dies on imbalance handling + honest metrics, and that multi-temporal change (TLS here, InSAR for TRINETRA) is the detection substrate.

title: Deep-Learning-Based Precipitation Nowcasting with Ground Weather Station Data and Radar Data
relevance_component: fuse SPARSE ground-station obs with radar -> +5.7% CSI heavy-rain 1-6h nowcast
takeaway: Most DL precip-nowcasting uses only radar/satellite images and ignores SPARSE ground-station observations; proposes ASOC, an attentive module capturing temporal dynamics + contextual relations among multiple weather stations, bolt-on to any image-based nowcaster without architecture change; improves CSI for HEAVY (>=10mm/hr) and light (>=1mm/hr) rain at 1-6h lead by 5.7% (South Korea 2014-2020). For TRINETRA #1/#7/candidate-#7/A3: TRINETRA fuses SPARSE IoT ground sensors with satellite precip (GPM) - this is direct evidence that attentively fusing sparse ground stations with gridded radar/satellite measurably improves HEAVY-rain nowcasting at exactly the 1-6h lead that drives flash-flood/cloudburst warnings; a concrete architecture for TRINETRA's rainfall-forecast branch and partial mitigation of the rainfall-forecast spatial-error risk (candidate #7) by anchoring the grid to ground truth.

title: Auto-differentiable Ensemble Kalman Filters
relevance_component: AD-EnKF: EnKF state recovery + autodiff-learned surrogate dynamics for high-dim DA
takeaway: AD-EnKF blends ensemble Kalman filtering (scales to high-dim state recovery) with automatic differentiation to TRAIN high-dim surrogate models of UNKNOWN state-space dynamics; outperforms EM/particle-filter hybrids on Lorenz-96, easy to implement, minimal tuning. For TRINETRA physics-gate/#17/candidate-#5/A4: TRINETRA must sequentially estimate an evolving physical state (pore pressure, soil moisture, lake level) from PARTIAL + NOISY multi-sensor observations - canonical data assimilation; AD-EnKF is a principled way to (i) assimilate IoT+satellite streams into the physics state in real time, (ii) LEARN the parts of the dynamics the Iverson/Richards model gets wrong (bias-correct the physics gate) while staying Bayesian/uncertainty-aware; a concrete DA backbone that unifies the physics model with data rather than running them side-by-side.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting of InSAR Ground Deformation in Eastern Ireland
relevance_component: CNN-LSTM forecasts InSAR deformation; baselines DEFAULT TO PERSISTENCE; sparse->dense tensor
takeaway: Forecasts future ground deformation from SPARSE InSAR time-series by transforming sparse point measurements into a DENSE spatio-temporal tensor, enabling CV architectures; a hybrid CNN-LSTM learns spatial patterns + temporal dependencies, benchmarked against LightGBM + LASSO on Sentinel-1 (eastern Ireland). KEY: interpretability analysis shows the BASELINE models often DEFAULT TO SIMPLISTIC PERSISTENCE patterns, so you must beat a persistence baseline to claim real skill. For TRINETRA #1(core!)/candidate-#1/A1: this is the closest match to TRINETRA's InSAR-deformation-forecasting front-end AND it supplies the exact methodological warning behind risk-candidate #1 - a forecaster can look accurate merely by copying the last value (persistence); TRINETRA MUST benchmark its SSL-encoder forecast head against a persistence baseline (and LightGBM) or its deformation-prediction skill is unproven; also validates sparse->dense tensorization + CNN-LSTM as a sensible architecture for the Sentinel-1 branch.

title: Conformal Prediction Algorithms for Time Series Forecasting: Methods and Benchmarking
relevance_component: survey+benchmark of CP for time series; temporal dependence BREAKS exchangeability
takeaway: Critically surveys + benchmarks conformal-prediction methods for TIME-SERIES forecasting, where temporal dependence VIOLATES the exchangeability assumption that standard CP coverage guarantees need; categorizes solutions (relax exchangeability; treat independent-series collections as the unit; model residual dynamics; online algorithms that adapt to distribution shift for long-run coverage); benchmark (AutoARIMA base, large sales dataset, Winkler score) finds multi-step split-CP meets the 90% coverage target with best efficiency. For TRINETRA #13(core)/A8: TRINETRA's conformal 'guarantee' is applied to strongly TEMPORALLY-DEPENDENT sensor/forecast streams - exactly the exchangeability violation this flags - so vanilla split-conformal coverage is NOT valid as stated (reinforces bug #13); provides the menu of correct time-series CP variants to replace the overclaim with an honest, dependence-aware interval.

title: Adaptive Conformal Predictions for Time Series
relevance_component: ACI/AgACI online-adaptive CP maintains coverage under distribution shift (no exchangeability)
takeaway: Argues Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI, Gibbs & Candes 2021) is a sound procedure for time series with general dependency; theoretically analyses the learning-rate's effect on efficiency (exchangeable + autoregressive cases); proposes AgACI, a PARAMETER-FREE method building on ACI via online expert aggregation to adaptively maintain coverage under DISTRIBUTION SHIFT. For TRINETRA #13(core)/candidate-#6/A8: this is the concrete, parameter-free mechanism to give TRINETRA honest long-run coverage on NON-exchangeable, drifting sensor streams - online-adaptive conformal that self-corrects coverage as the monsoon/season/sensor-health distribution shifts; the direct fix for the conformal overclaim (#13) and for conformal-breaks-under-shift (candidate #6), pairing with the multi-source weighted-conformal direction already in the synthesis.

title: DLTTA: Dynamic Learning Rate for Test-time Adaptation on Cross-domain Medical Images
authors: Yang; Chen; Jiang; Liu; Cao; Heng; Dou
relevance_component: per-sample dynamic LR TTA; memory-bank discrepancy estimate for sequential shift
takeaway: Test-time adaptation (TTA) for cross-domain shift where data arrive SEQUENTIALLY and the shift scale changes over time; prior TTA uses a FIXED learning rate for all test samples (sub-optimal); DLTTA uses a memory-bank discrepancy estimate per test sample to dynamically modulate the weight-update size, giving the right adaptation degree per input; validated on retinal-OCT seg, histopath classification, prostate-MRI seg, beating SOTA TTA. For TRINETRA candidate-#5/#18/A14: TRINETRA faces exactly sequential, time-varying distribution shift (new catchments, season/climate drift) and must adapt the deployed model WITHOUT labels; DLTTA's principle - adapt MORE when the input is far from training distribution, LESS when near - is a concrete, label-free online adaptation recipe, and the per-sample discrepancy signal doubles as an OOD/novelty flag feeding the abstain/defer-to-physics path. CAUTION for a safety system: unbounded TTA can drift the model; adaptation must be bounded + monitored (ties to the CPD monitors 2201.07125/2602.07252).

title: Is Epistemic Uncertainty Faithfully Represented by Evidential Deep Learning Methods?
relevance_component: CRITICAL caveat: EDL second-order losses hard to optimize; epistemic uncertainty only RELATIVE
takeaway: Theoretical critique of evidential deep learning (EDL): EDL extends ERM to predict SECOND-ORDER distributions over outcomes and read off epistemic+aleatoric uncertainty, but this paper proves difficulties OPTIMIZING second-order loss functions and problems INTERPRETING the resulting epistemic measures - identifiability + convergence issues in second-order loss minimization, and the epistemic-uncertainty measure is RELATIVE not absolute (covers classification, regression, counts). For TRINETRA #13/candidate-#12/A8 (HONESTY BALANCE): tempers the earlier EDL recommendation (2309.13207/2604.06387) - EDL is cheap single-pass UQ, BUT its epistemic numbers must NOT be treated as calibrated absolute probabilities for alarm decisions; use EDL for RELATIVE ranking/OOD flagging and back critical thresholds with conformal (which has coverage guarantees). Prevents TRINETRA from substituting one overclaim (conformal #13) for another (over-trusting evidential epistemic uncertainty).

title: Towards Hyperparameter-free Policy Selection for Offline Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: BVFT hyperparameter-free value-function/policy selection; combine with OPE for continuous actions
takeaway: Tackles how to SELECT among policies/value-functions from different offline-RL training runs (crucial for hyperparameter tuning) without creating a chicken-and-egg of OPE-needs-its-own-hyperparameters; designs HYPERPARAMETER-FREE selection via BVFT (Xie-Jiang value-function-selection theory), effective on discrete Atari; for continuous actions combines BVFT+OPE to get the best of both, yielding a theoretically-grounded hyperparameter tuner for Q-based OPE. For TRINETRA #9/A5: TRINETRA's offline-RL alarm policy (CQL/IQL/TD3+BC) requires choosing WHICH trained policy to deploy from historical data - BVFT gives a principled, hyperparameter-free way to do that selection with guarantees, closing the 'how do we know the chosen alarm policy is actually best' gap (bug #9); pairs with HVE (2206.02000) and Offline-RL-without-OPE (2106.08909) as the honest policy-valuation toolkit. (Was on pending-verify list - ID+authors now confirmed, not guessed.)

title: SCOPE-RL: A Python Library for Offline Reinforcement Learning and Off-Policy Evaluation
authors: Kiyohara; Kishimoto; Kawakami; Kobayashi; Nakata; Saito
relevance_component: end-to-end offline-RL + OPE + OPS library; estimates full reward DISTRIBUTION + risk-return tradeoff
takeaway: Open-source Python library (SCOPE-RL) seamlessly integrating offline-RL training with OPE and off-policy SELECTION (OPS); emphasis on OPE modules with many estimators + robust evaluation-of-OPE protocols; estimates the ENTIRE reward DISTRIBUTION under a policy (not just point expected value) and presents the RISK-RETURN tradeoff, going beyond accuracy-only OPE. ID 2311.18206 + all 6 authors CONFIRMED on own abstract page (I had initially recalled the ID from memory, then verified it live - not guessed). For TRINETRA #9/A5 (TOOLING): a concrete, documented framework to IMPLEMENT the honest OPE + policy-selection workflow (alongside BVFT 2110.14000 / HVE 2206.02000) for the alarm policy on logged data; crucially its risk-return + full-distribution OPE is exactly right when miss cost=-100 dominates (you must evaluate TAIL/worst-case policy value, not mean return) - lowers the barrier to doing offline-RL evaluation properly instead of reporting only training-env PPO reward.

title: Hybrid stochastic-mechanical modeling of precipitation thresholds of shallow landslide initiation
relevance_component: derives ID thresholds from physics + stochastic params (not empirical fit); Ks/slope/suction sensitivities
takeaway: Proposes a HYBRID STOCHASTIC-MECHANICAL approach to compute rainfall intensity-duration (ID) thresholds for shallow-landslide initiation from a physically-based triggering model with selected parameters treated as correlated ALEATORY variables (Monte Carlo), rather than empirical curve-fitting; illustrated on Campania (Italy). Key sensitivities: (i) saturated hydraulic conductivity Ks dominates for HIGH-intensity storms; (ii) on STEEP slopes, pressure-head changes sharply shorten triggering timescale -> heavy reliance on INITIAL conditions; (iii) for long failure times (gentle slopes / low intensity) the evolving stress level (dry unit weight gamma_d) matters most. For TRINETRA #15/#3/#17/A4 (DIRECT): this is strong evidence that a SINGLE fixed empirical ID constant (TRINETRA's Caine/Dahal/Garhwal a*D^-b) is physically unjustified - the true threshold is a DISTRIBUTION controlled by local Ks, slope, suction, gamma_d; supports replacing the hard-coded ID constants (bug #15) with a physically-derived, locally-parameterised, uncertainty-bearing threshold, and explains WHY borrowed-region constants fail (parameter mismatch). Also validates coupling the physics gate with stochastic parameter uncertainty.

title: Knowledge-infused Deep Learning Enables Interpretable Landslide Forecasting
relevance_component: SSL encoder / forecasting head / physics gate
takeaway: Transformer (LFIT) forecasts landslide deformation using prior knowledge + multi-source data; validated on Three Gorges reservoir + Tibetan creep. Supports forecasting-vs-mapping novelty & interpretability requirement; both validation sites are CREEP, reinforcing Bug #7 brittle-failure transfer caveat.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting of InSAR Ground Deformation in Eastern Ireland
relevance_component: InSAR datacube / forecast-residual anomaly
takeaway: CNN-LSTM over densified InSAR tensor beats LGBM/LASSO; shows baselines collapse to persistence. Direct method for forecast-residual module; warns naive baselines look good via persistence — relevant to eval-rigor Bug #11.

title: InSAR Phase Denoising: A Review of Current Technologies and Future Directions
relevance_component: InSAR preprocessing
takeaway: Phase denoising is a mandatory step before deformation/forecasting; four method families. Missing denoising stage is a data-quality risk upstream of the SSL encoder.

title: A Real-time System for Detecting Landslide Reports on Social Media using AI
authors: Ofli; Qazi; Imran; Roch; Pennington; Banks; Bossu
relevance_component: opportunistic vision / crowd reports
takeaway: Operational Twitter landslide detector (dedup, image classify, geolocate). Supports an auxiliary crowd-report ingestion channel as a cheap redundant sensor; deployment-tested since 2020.

title: Hurricane Forecasting: A Novel Multimodal Machine Learning Framework (Hurricast)
relevance_component: meta-fusion head
takeaway: Combines deep encoder-decoder spatiotemporal features + gradient-boosted trees; consensus-model inclusion beats NHC official. Direct precedent for TRINETRA's encoder->XGBoost + stacked meta-fusion; evidence stacking helps operational skill.

title: A Survey on Offline Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: offline RL stage
takeaway: Survey centering distributional shift as THE core offline-RL failure; model-based methods use uncertainty penalties. Grounds why TRINETRA's offline-RL stage needs pessimism + OOD penalties, not just CQL default.

title: Do Satellite Tasks Need Special Pretraining?
authors: Vanyan; Barseghyan; Tamazyan; Galstyan; Huroyan; Hovakimyan; Khachatrian
relevance_component: SSL encoder benchmark
takeaway: At ViT-B scale, RS-specific foundation models bring NO consistent gain over general-purpose vision encoders on low-res generalization. Challenges TRINETRA's bespoke SSL encoder claim; demands a general-purpose baseline comparison (reinforces Bug #18 under-benchmarking).

title: MAPEX: Modality-Aware Pruning of Experts for Remote Sensing Foundation Models
relevance_component: SSL encoder / MoE gating
takeaway: MoE RS foundation model with modality-aware expert routing; prunes experts per task modality. Directly informs TRINETRA's gated meta-fusion (modality-aware gating) + addresses modality mismatch of generic FMs.

title: RiverMamba: A State Space Model for Global River Discharge and Flood Forecasting
relevance_component: flood forecasting / lead time
takeaway: Mamba SSM forecasts global river discharge + floods on 0.05deg grid up to 7-day lead, beating AI + physics baselines incl. extreme return periods. SOTA alternative/benchmark for TRINETRA's flood channel; lead-time framing informs RL reward design.

title: Leveraging Approximate Model-based Shielding for Probabilistic Safety Guarantees in Continuous Environments
relevance_component: safety shield
takeaway: Extends approximate model-based shielding to continuous state/action with probabilistic safety guarantees + policy-gradient penalties. Upgrades TRINETRA's hard shield from discrete thresholds to continuous probabilistic guarantee; relevant to shield correctness.

title: Explanations for Unrealizability of Infinite-State Safety Shields
relevance_component: safety shield
takeaway: Shields can be UNREALIZABLE when the spec is inconsistent/contradictory; gives unrolling-based explanations. Critical: TRINETRA's shield rules (FS<1->Orange, tilt->Red, rain->Orange, GLOF->Red) could contradict -> must check realizability (new risk).

title: Robust Conformal Prediction Using Privileged Information
relevance_component: conformal calibration
takeaway: Naive conformal fails under missing/noisy training variables; builds coverage robust to such corruption. TRINETRA's sensor dropouts (brownout, Bug #8) break i.i.d.; this is a fix path for the conformal overclaim (Bug #13).

title: Who Moved My Distribution? Conformal Prediction for Interactive Multi-Agent Systems
relevance_component: conformal / endogenous shift
takeaway: Iterative conformal adapts to endogenous distribution shift (acting changes the distribution). TRINETRA alarms change human behavior (evacuation) -> endogenous shift on future data; marginal conformal coverage not preserved. New subtlety for Bug #13.

title: A Lightweight Video Anomaly Detection Model with Weak Supervision and Adaptive Instance Selection
relevance_component: River Eye / CCTV VAD
takeaway: Weakly-supervised VAD (video-level labels only) with small model + adaptive instance selection. Matches TRINETRA's label-scarce edge CCTV; weak supervision is realistic vs frame-level labels. Supports edge-VAD feasibility (Bug #14).

title: Quo Vadis, Anomaly Detection? LLMs and VLMs in the Spotlight
relevance_component: CCTV VAD survey
takeaway: Review of 2024 LLM/VLM VAD: interpretability, temporal reasoning, few/zero-shot, open-world anomalies. Maps the VAD design space + zero-shot option for unseen hazard appearances on River Eye nodes.

title: Class Distribution Monitoring for Concept Drift Detection
relevance_component: deployment monitoring
takeaway: CDM monitors class-conditional distributions via QuantTree change detection; controls Average Run Length (ARL0 = expected time to false alarm). Directly gives TRINETRA a principled sensor-drift monitor with FA-rate control -> fix for Bug #8 brownout/drift.

title: STUDD: A Student-Teacher Method for Unsupervised Concept Drift Detection
relevance_component: deployment monitoring (no labels)
takeaway: Unsupervised drift detection via student mimicking teacher; monitors student-teacher disagreement, needs NO true labels. Landslides are rare so labels are unavailable in real time -> STUDD is the right drift monitor for TRINETRA. Strong fix for Bug #8.

title: LPWA-MAC: a Low Power Wide Area network MAC protocol for cyber-physical systems
relevance_component: LoRa MAC / bounded delay
takeaway: LPWAN MAC giving bounded end-to-end delay + high channel utility for CPS control (vs delay-tolerant monitoring). Relevant to TRINETRA alarm-grade latency guarantees over LoRa, beyond best-effort; informs Bug #6/#8 comms realism.

title: Qualitative Assessment of Low Power Wide Area Network Protocols and their Security Aspect
relevance_component: LoRa protocol/security
takeaway: Compares LoRaWAN/NB-IoT/Sigfox incl. security; LoRaWAN best for sparse long-battery-life sensor nets. Supports LoRaWAN choice but flags security surface -> ties to Proxy credential-leak Bug #12 (comms security hygiene).

title: Selection of contributing factors for predicting landslide susceptibility using ML and DL
relevance_component: feature selection / anomaly inputs
takeaway: Systematic factor-selection (IGR/RFE/PSO/LASSO/HHO + autoencoder) effect on LS prediction accuracy; no universally best method. Grounds TRINETRA's input-feature choices + warns feature-selection is dataset-specific (generalization caveat, Bug #11).

title: A Complete Characterization of Linear Estimators for Offline Policy Evaluation
relevance_component: offline policy evaluation
takeaway: Necessary+sufficient conditions for FQI/LSTD to succeed at OPE; many strong negative results -> OPE often intractable. CRITICAL caveat: TRINETRA cannot trust naive offline value estimates of its alarm policy; OPE may be invalid (new eval risk, extends Bug #11).

title: Event Detection in Time Series: Universal Deep Learning Approach
relevance_component: rare-event detection
takeaway: Regression-based (not binary-classification) event detector handles rare events + imbalance + interval events in one framework. Alternative formulation for TRINETRA's rare-hazard detection; avoids per-timestep binary-label pathology.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-class Imbalanced Training
relevance_component: imbalance / RL reward
takeaway: Dueling+double DQN with custom reward for extreme multi-class imbalance; RL agent learns minority-sensitive policy. Supports casting TRINETRA's rare-alarm problem as cost-sensitive RL; informs reward shaping (Bug #9) under imbalance.

title: Prioritizing emergency evacuations under compounding levels of uncertainty
relevance_component: evacuation / alarm policy
takeaway: MDP evacuation-prioritization under 3 nested uncertainty levels; optimized MDP beats 8 heuristics; extra model-uncertainty layers add complexity w/o gain. Validates MDP alarm policy + warns against over-modeling uncertainty (relevant to RL stage + Bug #11 parsimony).

title: Data-Driven Bayesian Network Models of Hurricane Evacuation Decision Making
relevance_component: people-at-risk / human response
takeaway: Bayesian networks model real evacuation decisions from hurricane questionnaires; compliance is probabilistic, not guaranteed. TRINETRA's people-at-risk + disruption reward assumes compliance; this shows real human response is stochastic -> calibrate 'people actually evacuated' (reward realism, Bug #9).

title: Tighter Risk Bounds for Mixtures of Experts
relevance_component: MoE gating / generalization
takeaway: Generalization risk bounds for one-out-of-n (hard) gating MoE; log dependence on #experts. Theory backing TRINETRA's gated meta-fusion generalization; argues for sparse hard gating over dense gating (design choice justification).

title: On Bayesian Softmax-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Models
relevance_component: MoE gating / model selection
takeaway: Posterior contraction + model-selection consistency for softmax-gated MoE incl. learnable #experts. Grounds choosing #experts in TRINETRA's GMF head + Bayesian treatment of gate; supports principled expert-count selection.

title: On Uncertainty Prediction for Deep-Learning-based Particle Image Velocimetry
relevance_component: LSPIV / River Eye uncertainty
takeaway: UQ for DL-PIV via uncertainty NN / multi-model / multi-transform; UNN best; UQ 'largely overlooked'. TRINETRA's River Eye LSPIV reports discharge with NO uncertainty -> this gives the missing per-measurement UQ (new gap -> River Eye reliability).

title: Variational Auto-Encoder Based Deep Learning Technique For Filling Gaps in Reacting PIV Data
relevance_component: LSPIV gap-filling
takeaway: CVAE fills gaps/dropouts in PIV vector fields. River Eye nodes will have occlusion/night/turbidity gaps; this is a method to impute missing LSPIV velocity rather than drop frames (robustness for Bug #8 brownout).

title: A Review on Self-Supervised Learning for Time Series Anomaly Detection
relevance_component: SSL anomaly head
takeaway: Survey: unsupervised AD overfits known normal + fails to adapt to unseen normality; SSL pretext tasks help. Directly scopes TRINETRA's SSL-encoder+anomaly design space and warns the normal boundary is often too tight -> FA risk (ties Bug #1 thresholds).

title: CARLA: Self-supervised Contrastive Representation Learning for Time Series Anomaly Detection
relevance_component: SSL anomaly head
takeaway: Contrastive SSL for TSAD; tight normal boundaries cause high FP + poor generalization; CARLA learns richer normal reps. Concrete SOTA method + the exact FP pathology TRINETRA risks; informs anomaly-module choice & FA control.

title: Likelihood-based Out-of-Distribution Detection with Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
relevance_component: OOD gating
takeaway: Complexity-corrected likelihood ratio for OOD with diffusion models. Option for TRINETRA to flag OOD sensor inputs (novel storm regimes) before trusting the encoder; gate on OOD (robustness).

title: Towards Robust Deep Learning using Entropic Losses
relevance_component: OOD rejection
takeaway: Entropic losses + detection scores let a net 'know the unknown' and reject OOD inputs; also calibrates probabilities. TRINETRA should reject-and-defer to physics/shield on OOD rather than emit a confident anomaly; supports fail-safe design.

title: On Uniformly Scaling Flows: A Density-Aligned Approach to Deep One-Class Classification
relevance_component: Deep SVDD anomaly head
takeaway: Proves uniformly-scaling normalizing flows reduce to a Deep SVDD objective with collapse-preventing regularization; drop-in replacement improves stability+accuracy. TRINETRA uses Deep SVDD -> this is a direct upgrade that fixes representational-collapse risk (anomaly-module robustness).

title: Audio-based Anomaly Detection in Industrial Machines Using Deep One-Class SVDD
relevance_component: Deep SVDD validation
takeaway: Deep SVDD on cheap microphone sensors for condition monitoring. Analogue to TRINETRA's cheap-sensor ethos; shows Deep SVDD works on low-cost acoustic signals (supports cheap-node anomaly detection).

title: Monitoring surface deformation over oilfield using MT-InSAR and production well data
relevance_component: SBAS InSAR baseline
takeaway: SBAS multi-temporal InSAR resolves ~13.5 mm/yr subsidence, cross-validated vs production data. Methodological reference for TRINETRA's SBAS deformation-velocity estimation + external cross-validation practice.

title: Deep learning networks for selection of persistent scatterer pixels in MT-InSAR
relevance_component: InSAR PS selection
takeaway: CNN-ISS + CLSTM-ISS learn to select PS pixels vs conventional noise/look-angle criteria. A learned front-end for TRINETRA's InSAR pipeline; improves PS density/quality -> better deformation precursors. Also shows DL can replace hand-tuned PS thresholds.

title: Deep Learning for Precipitation Nowcasting: A Benchmark and A New Model (TrajGRU)
authors: Shi; Gao; Lausen; Wang; Yeung; Wong; Woo
relevance_component: precip nowcasting input
takeaway: TrajGRU learns location-variant recurrence, beats ConvLSTM; HKO benchmark + eval protocol. Canonical precipitation-nowcasting method + proper eval protocol; a candidate for TRINETRA's rainfall-forecast input and a benchmark discipline (Bug #11).

title: Precipitation Nowcasting using Deep Neural Network
relevance_component: precip nowcasting input
takeaway: DNN precipitation nowcasting (fast vs NWP). Secondary reference for TRINETRA's near-real-time rainfall input; nowcasting is faster but shorter-horizon than NWP (lead-time tradeoff informs RL reward).

title: A Survey of Protocols for Intermittently Connected Delay-Tolerant Wireless Sensor Networks
relevance_component: DTN / store-and-forward
takeaway: Survey of ICDT-WSN protocols: WSN+DTN hybrid for intermittently connected sensor nets; store-carry-forward. TRINETRA's offline-first LoRa nodes ARE an ICDT-WSN; this maps the right protocol family + warns pure-WSN/pure-DTN protocols are inadequate (comms-design, Bug #6/#8).

title: From Rules to Rewards: Reinforcement Learning for Interest Rate Adjustment in DeFi Lending
relevance_component: offline RL stage (TD3-BC)
takeaway: Compares CQL vs BC vs TD3-BC on real Aave data; TD3-BC best at balancing utilization/stability/risk + robust to stress events. Empirical support for TRINETRA's TD3-BC choice over plain CQL; stress-event robustness analogy to rare hazards.

title: Conservative DDPG -- Pessimistic RL without Ensemble
relevance_component: offline RL pessimism
takeaway: Adds a BC-loss penalty + Q-target to DDPG as a cheap uncertainty/pessimism measure; beats DDPG, competitive w/ TD3, far less compute. A lightweight pessimistic offline-RL option fitting TRINETRA's Kaggle compute budget (Bug on compute realism).

title: Sim-and-Real Reinforcement Learning for Manipulation: A Consensus-based Approach
relevance_component: simulator PPO stage / sim-to-real
takeaway: Finds best-in-sim policy is NOT best for sim-and-real; more sim agents helps. Direct caution for TRINETRA's SB3-PPO-in-simulator stage: optimizing sim reward can hurt real deployment -> validates need for sim-to-real care (new RL risk).

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Traffic Forecasting: A Unified Approach (DeepSTUQ)
relevance_component: calibration / UQ
takeaway: Separates aleatoric vs epistemic UQ for spatio-temporal forecasting + Temperature-Scaling post-calibration. Template for TRINETRA to report calibrated aleatoric+epistemic uncertainty on its forecasts, not a bare point estimate (fix path for Bug #13 overclaim).

title: Feature Guided Masked Autoencoder for Self-supervised Learning in Remote Sensing (FG-MAE)
relevance_component: SSL encoder / SAR MAE
takeaway: MAE over-focuses on pixel detail -> weak semantics esp. for noisy SAR; FG-MAE reconstructs HOG(+NDI) instead, big boost for SAR. DIRECT caution for TRINETRA's masked-modeling InSAR/SAR encoder: raw-pixel MAE is suboptimal on SAR -> use feature targets (encoder-design fix).

title: FireRisk: A Remote Sensing Dataset for Fire Risk Assessment with SSL Benchmarks
relevance_component: SSL hazard benchmark
takeaway: GIS-based hazard models hard to scale across geographies due to data/local-condition variation; SSL on free RS helps. Reinforces TRINETRA's generalization-across-regions risk (Uttarakhand->Himachal transfer, Bug #11/#18) + SSL baseline practice.

title: CSMAE: Cross-Sensor Masked Autoencoders for Remote Sensing Image Retrieval
relevance_component: cross-sensor SSL
takeaway: Systematic study of masked image modeling for uni-/cross-modal RS retrieval; derives design guideline. Grounds TRINETRA's cross-sensor (S1/S2) SSL fusion design choices.

title: An investigation of the Brumadinho Dam Break with HEC-RAS simulation
relevance_component: dam-break / runout inundation
takeaway: HEC-RAS mudflow model on SRTM DEM reproduces observed Brumadinho tailings-dam flood extent. Validates DEM-driven inundation modeling TRINETRA needs for GLOF/dam-break downstream mapping; a concrete runout-extent method + validation (supports physics-gate inundation).

title: Data-driven and ML-based prediction of wave propagation behavior in dam-break flood
relevance_component: dam-break surrogate
takeaway: Reservoir-computing (RC-ESN) surrogate for 1D dam-break Saint-Venant dynamics from minimal data. A fast ML surrogate for flood-wave propagation -> could give TRINETRA real-time GLOF arrival-time estimates vs expensive solver (edge-compute fit).

title: DCER: Dual-Stage Compression and Energy-Based Reconstruction for Multimodal Fusion
relevance_component: missing-modality fusion
takeaway: Energy-based reconstruction recovers missing modalities + yields intrinsic uncertainty (rho>0.72 w/ error); U-shaped robustness. Directly addresses TRINETRA sensor-dropout: recover missing sat/CCTV/IoT stream + get uncertainty flag (strong fix for Bug #8).

title: RoHyDR: Robust Hybrid Diffusion Recovery for Incomplete Multimodal
relevance_component: missing-modality fusion
takeaway: Diffusion-based recovery of missing modalities at unimodal/multimodal/feature/semantic levels. Second method for TRINETRA to degrade gracefully when a sensor layer drops out rather than failing (robustness alternative to DCER).

title: Safe Continual Reinforcement Learning Methods for Nonstationary Environments: A Survey
relevance_component: safe RL under nonstationarity
takeaway: Survey of continual safe online RL under nonstationarity (NSMDP/HM-MDP/safe POMDP), safety-constraint taxonomy. TRINETRA's climate is nonstationary + policy must stay safe while adapting -> frames the exact COSRL problem + catalogs mechanisms (grounds shield+adaptation design, Bug #9 + drift).

title: CAPSULE: Control-Theoretic Action Perturbations for Safe Uncertainty-Aware RL
relevance_component: safe RL hard constraints
takeaway: Hard (not in-expectation) safety via control-theoretic action perturbation; integrates w/ SAC/TD3; up to 126x fewer violations. Supports TRINETRA's hard safety-shield philosophy over expectation-only guarantees; concrete mechanism for the alarm shield (Bug #9 fix path).

title: Conformal Prediction for Time Series with Modern Hopfield Networks (HopCPT)
relevance_component: conformal under autocorrelation
takeaway: Autocorrelation in time series VIOLATES conformal exchangeability; HopCPT copes with+leverages temporal structure. Directly addresses TRINETRA's conformal overclaim (Bug #13): naive CP invalid on autocorrelated sensor streams -> use time-series CP.

title: Flow-based Conformal Prediction for Multi-dimensional Time Series
relevance_component: conformal multi-dim
takeaway: Conformal for multi-dim TS via flow + classifier-free guidance; non-asymptotic marginal + finite-sample conditional coverage despite non-exchangeability. Rigorous CP option for TRINETRA's multi-sensor vector forecasts (fix path, Bug #13).

title: Cross-Polarization Fusion of VV and VH SAR Observations for Improved Flood Mapping
relevance_component: SAR flood extent
takeaway: VV+VH fusion beats single-pol SAR for flood mapping, esp. vegetated/heterogeneous terrain. TRINETRA should fuse both Sentinel-1 polarizations for flood-extent, not single-pol; concrete accuracy gain + Himalaya vegetation relevance.

title: Urban Flood Mapping Using Satellite SAR Data: A Review
relevance_component: SAR flood review
takeaway: Review of SAR urban-flood methods/datasets; SAR all-weather day-night advantage + method-selection guidance. Scopes TRINETRA's SAR flood-mapping choices + known failure modes (layover/shadow in terrain) relevant to Himalayan valleys.

title: Learning Displacement-Robust Representations for Landslide Early Warning under Rainfall Forecast Uncertainty (RMCL)
relevance_component: LEWS forecast-uncertainty robustness
takeaway: MOST landslide predictors assume ACCURATE rainfall; operational LEWS use FORECASTS with spatial displacement that degrades accuracy. RMCL contrastive learning gives displacement-robust reps, +37% precision over SOTA across 19 Japan regions. CRITICAL: TRINETRA's physics gate + anomaly head likely assume accurate rainfall -> forecast displacement is an unmodeled failure mode (NEW BUG CANDIDATE + fix).

title: Foundation Models Meet Agriculture: Challenges Beyond Pretraining
relevance_component: EO FM modality gap
takeaway: EO foundation models yield 'surprisingly poor' results on specialized downstream tasks: pretraining-deployment modality gap (can't ingest non-imagery) + unstable rankings across settings. Reinforces Bug #18: a bespoke/off-the-shelf EO-FM may NOT transfer to TRINETRA's multimodal hazard task; benchmark instability warning (#11).

title: REOBench: Benchmarking Robustness of Earth Observation Foundation Models
relevance_component: EO FM robustness
takeaway: Benchmarks robustness of EO foundation models under corruptions/perturbations. Gives TRINETRA a robustness-eval protocol for its satellite encoder under noise/cloud/sensor degradation (test discipline, Bug #11).

title: PhilEO Bench: Evaluating Geo-Spatial Foundation Models
authors: Fibaek; Camilleri; Luyts; Dionelis; Le Saux
relevance_component: EO FM benchmark
takeaway: Testbed + 400GB Sentinel-2 dataset to evaluate FMs (Prithvi, SatMAE) at multiple n-shots. A concrete few-shot EO-FM benchmark TRINETRA could use to justify (or refute) its encoder choice vs Prithvi/SatMAE (Bug #18 benchmarking).

title: Interpretable Anomaly Detection with DIFFI: Depth-based Isolation Forest Feature Importance
relevance_component: isolation forest interpretability
takeaway: Isolation Forest lacks interpretability; DIFFI gives global/local feature importance + unsupervised feature selection. TRINETRA uses isolation forest in its ensemble -> DIFFI makes its anomaly scores explainable to operators (trust/ops fix) + feature selection.

title: Improved Anomaly Detection by Using the Attention-Based Isolation Forest (ABIForest)
relevance_component: isolation forest upgrade
takeaway: Attention-weighted isolation forest improves AD over vanilla IF. Direct upgrade option for TRINETRA's isolation-forest ensemble member (anomaly-module robustness).

title: Inverse analysis of granular flows using differentiable graph neural network simulator
relevance_component: runout surrogate (BASELINE-dup)
takeaway: NOTE: already in local corpus; deduped, NOT counted as new. Differentiable GNS for granular-flow inverse runout; baffle design. Listed only to mark dedup.

title: Modeling liquefaction-induced runout of a tailings dam using hybrid FEM-MPM
relevance_component: runout physics
takeaway: Hybrid finite-element + material-point method for liquefaction-induced flow-slide runout. High-fidelity runout reference relevant to TRINETRA's debris/mud runout modeling (physics-gate validation anchor; MPM for large deformation).

title: UCF-Crime-DVS: Event-Based Dataset for VAD with Spiking Neural Networks
authors: Qian; Ye; Wang; Cai; Qian; Wu
relevance_component: edge VAD / event camera
takeaway: Event-camera (DVS) + spiking-NN VAD: high dynamic range, low data redundancy, efficient. Alt sensing+compute path for TRINETRA's edge CCTV where power/bandwidth constrained; SNN energy efficiency relevant to #14 edge-latency.

title: Generative Cooperative Learning for Unsupervised Video Anomaly Detection
relevance_component: unsupervised VAD
takeaway: Unsupervised VAD (no labels) via generative cooperative learning; anomalies rare + ill-defined. Matches TRINETRA's label-scarce CCTV reality (no curated hazard-video labels) -> unsupervised VAD is the realistic setting (#14, supports label-free edge VAD).

title: Automatic Learning to Detect Concept Drift (Meta-ADD)
relevance_component: drift-type classification
takeaway: Meta-ADD learns to CLASSIFY the TYPE of concept drift (not just detect magnitude) via prototypical net + stream active learning. TRINETRA needs to know WHICH drift (seasonal vs regime vs sensor fault) to react correctly -> drift-type awareness upgrades the drift monitor (extends #8 fix).

title: Learner-based Concept Drift Detection: Analysis and Evaluation
relevance_component: drift detector eval
takeaway: Theoretical+empirical evaluation of many drift-detection algorithms on synthetic+real streams. Gives TRINETRA an evidence base to pick a drift detector + eval protocol (test discipline for #8).

title: Regularized boosting as meta-learner in HPO stacking ensemble
relevance_component: stacked-generalization meta-learner
takeaway: Stacking meta-learners can suffer MULTICOLLINEARITY among base-model predictions; boosting meta-learner removes it; Caruana method also robust. DIRECT caution for TRINETRA's GMF stacked head: correlated experts (all seeing same storm) induce multicollinearity -> meta-head instability (NEW RISK for GMF + concrete fix: boosting/Caruana meta-learner).

title: Beacon-based uplink transmission for LoRaWAN direct-to-satellite IoT
relevance_component: LoRa-to-satellite backhaul
takeaway: Class-B-synchronized uplink from ground LoRaWAN devices to LEO satellite gateways; ~2x traffic vs standard. Backhaul option for TRINETRA nodes in valleys with NO terrestrial gateway -> direct-to-satellite LoRa for truly isolated sites (comms-robustness, extends #6).

title: D2D Communications in LoRaWAN LPWAN: From Idea to Empirical Validation
relevance_component: LoRa device-to-device
takeaway: Device-to-device over LoRaWAN LPWAN, empirically validated. Supports TRINETRA node-to-node relaying when gateway unreachable (mesh/relay robustness for offline-first design, #6/#8).

title: Predicting extreme events from data using deep machine learning: when and where
relevance_component: extreme-event space-time prediction
takeaway: DCNN predicts extreme events in time (when) + space (where) from 2D image snapshots; notes spatial bias in event occurrence HURTS accuracy. Template for TRINETRA's when/where hazard forecasting from image stacks + warning about spatially biased training data (ties class-imbalance #9 + #11 eval).

title: UniExtreme: A Universal Foundation Model for Extreme Weather Forecasting
relevance_component: extreme-weather FM
takeaway: FM with learnable Beta-distribution spectral filters + region-specific Event-Prior Augmentation; beats SOTA on extreme + general weather. Candidate upstream weather input for TRINETRA + region-prior idea maps to Himalaya-specific priors (input + #18 prior art).

title: Design of GNSS-RTK Landslide Monitoring System Based on Improved Raida Criterion
relevance_component: ground IoT deformation node
takeaway: Raspberry-Pi + GNSS-RTK + NB-IoT node; improved-Raida (3-sigma) gross-error rejection + Butterworth low-pass + edge compute -> 10mm real-time deformation. DIRECT comparator for TRINETRA's ground IoT: shows a REALISTIC cheap edge node + the gross-error/noise filtering TRINETRA's BOM omits (hardening #7/#8; cost realism).

title: Towards Open Science: Monitoring Crustal Deformations in North America (GNSS)
relevance_component: GNSS network processing
takeaway: Large-scale GNSS time-series processing to detect long-wavelength + subtle strain across a network. Methodology for TRINETRA to exploit regional GNSS networks (not just single stations) for deformation context (satellite/ground fusion).

title: Evacuation Planning for Disaster Preparedness: An Adaptive Robust Optimization Approach
relevance_component: evacuation under uncertainty
takeaway: First adaptive-robust model jointly optimizing shelter location + route + supply prepositioning under worst-case evacuee uncertainty. TRINETRA emits alarms but the DOWNSTREAM evacuation plan must handle uncertain evacuee counts -> robust-optimization layer complements the people-at-risk estimate (decision-layer completeness).

title: Ridesharing Evacuation Model of Disaster Response
relevance_component: evacuation logistics
takeaway: MIP ridesharing evacuation; counterintuitively, more vehicles for carless isn't always most efficient; strategy varies by disaster scale. Nuance for TRINETRA's disruption-cost term: evacuation efficiency is nonlinear in resources -> informs RL disruption penalty realism (#9/#11).

title: Series2Vec: Similarity-based Self-supervised Representation Learning for Time Series Classification
relevance_component: SSL time-series encoder
takeaway: TS SSL is fundamentally different from vision/NLP; contrastive positive-sample risk; Series2Vec predicts temporal+spectral similarity, no hand-crafted augmentation, matches supervised w/ limited labels. Direct guidance for TRINETRA's sensor-stream SSL: naive contrastive aug may hurt -> similarity-based SSL better for geophysical TS (encoder design, ties #18).

title: Time Series Generation with Masked Autoencoder (ExtraMAE)
relevance_component: MAE time-series synthesis
takeaway: Masked-autoencoder generates synthetic time series via self-supervision. Relevant to TRINETRA both as SSL-encoder validation and as a data-augmentation route for rare-hazard sequences (ties #9 imbalance + SSL design).

title: Correcting Class Imbalance in Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Tabular Classification
relevance_component: imbalance: thresholding
takeaway: Under class imbalance, THRESHOLDING works exceptionally well due to PFN calibration; downsampling comparable + cheaper; loss-based strategies impossible in ICL. Supports TRINETRA's threshold-tuning approach for rare hazards IF the model is well-calibrated -> links calibration (#13) to threshold choice (#1).

title: SeismoFlow -- Data augmentation for the class imbalance problem
relevance_component: imbalance: generative aug
takeaway: Glow-based flow generative model interpolates latent space to synthesize rare-class seismograms for imbalance. A concrete generative-augmentation path for TRINETRA's rare geophysical signals (seismic/tilt) -> mitigates #9 imbalance; geophysical domain match.

title: Evaluation of Active Feature Acquisition Methods for Time-varying Feature Settings
relevance_component: cost-aware sensing + shift
takeaway: Deploying a feature-acquisition agent itself TRIGGERS distribution shift; proposes AFAPE evaluation under NDE/NUC assumptions. CRITICAL analogy: TRINETRA's RL deciding when to query expensive sensors/alarms CHANGES the data distribution it later sees -> endogenous shift in evaluation (reinforces #11 OPE + #8 shift).

title: High-Resolution Forest Mapping from L-Band Interferometric SAR Time Series using Deep Learning
relevance_component: InSAR coherence features
takeaway: Adding InSAR COHERENCE layers + model-based inverted features beats backscatter-intensity-only; attention/nested UNet beats vanilla+classic ML; L-band guidance for NISAR/ROSE-L. TRINETRA should feed coherence (not just amplitude/phase) + use attention fusion; L-band relevance for future NISAR over Himalaya (encoder-input design, #18).

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting of InSAR Ground Deformation in Eastern Ireland
relevance_component: InSAR deformation FORECASTING
takeaway: Transforms SPARSE InSAR points -> dense spatio-temporal tensor, then CNN-LSTM forecasts future deformation; beats LightGBM/LASSO which default to naive PERSISTENCE. DIRECTLY validates TRINETRA's InSAR-forecasting premise AND exposes a key risk: baselines/forecasters often collapse to persistence -> TRINETRA must prove it beats persistence (NEW eval requirement, ties #11/#18).

title: Improving the Effectiveness of Potential-Based Reward Shaping in RL
relevance_component: reward shaping robustness
takeaway: Potential-based reward shaping (PBRS) is policy-invariant + significantly more ROBUST TO SCALING than typical reward shaping -> easier to tune. DIRECT guidance for Bug #9: TRINETRA's hand-tuned reward magnitudes (miss=-100, FA=-5...) are brittle; PBRS-style shaping would be scale-robust + preserve optimal policy (fix path for reward design).

title: Subgoal-based Reward Shaping to Improve Efficiency in Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: reward shaping / subgoals
takeaway: Subgoal-based reward shaping lets humans inject knowledge via representative states; beats potential-based + naive baselines on efficiency. Option for TRINETRA to encode escalation subgoals (watch->warn->evacuate) as shaped rewards (RL design, #9).

title: Comparison of two early warning systems for regional flash flood hazard forecasting
authors: Corral; Berenguer; Sempere-Torres; Poletti; Silvestro; Rebora
relevance_component: flash-flood EWS comparison
takeaway: Compares rainfall-based (ERICHA) vs distributed rainfall-runoff (Flood-PROOFS) flash-flood EWS on Liguria; agree for large catchments/return periods, DIVERGE for small catchments. CRITICAL for TRINETRA's small Himalayan catchments: simple rainfall-threshold vs full hydrology DIVERGE exactly in the small, steep basins TRINETRA targets (validates physics-gate necessity, #11).

title: FlowDB: a large scale precipitation
takeaway: ABS
column12: Large-scale precip+river+flash-flood dataset (no prior dataset existed for ML flash-flood forecasting). A concrete external benchmark TRINETRA could use to pretrain/evaluate its flash-flood head beyond its own region (addresses #11 underpowered eval + #18 benchmarking).

title: Flow-based SVDD for anomaly detection (FlowSVDD)
authors: Sendera; Smieja; Maziarka; Struski; Spurek; Tabor
relevance_component: Deep SVDD collapse fix
takeaway: Standard Deep SVDD can COLLAPSE the bounding hypersphere to a point (degenerate solution); FlowSVDD uses flow-based models to naturally PREVENT collapse + beats related deep-SVDD methods. DIRECT caution+fix for TRINETRA's Deep SVDD ensemble member: hypersphere-collapse is a known failure -> use anti-collapse variant (anomaly-module robustness).

title: Predictive Safety Shield for Dyna-Q Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: predictive safety shield
takeaway: Existing shields use random safe-action sampling / fixed fallback, IGNORING future performance of safe actions; predictive shield updates Q locally from safe model simulation -> keeps hard guarantees AND improves performance; robust to sim-to-real shift w/o retraining. DIRECT upgrade for TRINETRA's shield (Bug #9): its hard overrides are a fixed fallback that ignores downstream cost -> predictive shield picks the best SAFE escalation.

title: Safety-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Latent Shielding
relevance_component: latent shielding high-dim
takeaway: Latent shielding enables safe deep RL in HIGH-dimensional envs without a hand-crafted model, learning safety in latent space. Relevant to TRINETRA's high-dim sensor state where a tabular shield is infeasible -> latent-space safety option (shield scalability, #9).

title: Detecting Signs of Model Change with Continuous Model Selection (Descriptive Dimensionality)
relevance_component: early change-sign detection
takeaway: Descriptive dimensionality (Ddim) tracks real-valued model complexity to raise EARLY-WARNING of model/regime change BEFORE it fully actualizes. For TRINETRA: an early-warning drift signal that fires before the hazard model degrades -> proactive retraining trigger (extends #8 drift monitor to pre-emptive).

title: A finite element method using a bounded auxiliary variable for solving the Richards equation
relevance_component: Richards eq. numerics
takeaway: Stable FEM for Richards equation handling BOTH dry and fully-saturated zones + LAYERED soils without regularization; van Genuchten/Haverkamp. TRINETRA's Iverson transient model is a LINEARIZED approximation; this is the full-fidelity reference showing layered-soil + wetting-front dynamics the linearization omits (grounds physics-gate limits, ties #3 Iverson scope).

title: Modeling of unsaturated flow through porous media using meshless methods
relevance_component: unsaturated flow numerics
takeaway: Meshless Richards-equation solver for infiltration in porous media. Secondary numerical reference for unsaturated infiltration (physics-gate fidelity context, #3).

title: CIDOR: Content Distribution and Retrieval in Disaster Networks for Public Protection
relevance_component: ICN+DTN disaster comms
takeaway: Information-Centric Networking over DTN for disaster comms; retrieves content by name regardless of location; cuts retrieval time ~50%, response ~100%. Architecture pattern for TRINETRA's offline-first alert dissemination when infrastructure is down (comms-robustness, #6/#8).

title: Evaluating Opportunistic Routing Protocols in a Disaster Scenario (2016 Central Italy earthquake)
relevance_component: DTN opportunistic routing eval
takeaway: Evaluates opportunistic/DTN routing protocols in a realistic post-earthquake disaster scenario with mixed mobile/static nodes + responders. Empirical guidance for choosing TRINETRA's store-carry-forward routing when gateways fail (comms-robustness eval, #6/#8).

title: Strategizing Equitable Transit Evacuations: A Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning Approach
relevance_component: equitable evacuation RL
takeaway: Models bus evacuation as an MDP solved by RL using real GTFS transit + OSM networks; dynamically reroutes buses to minimize total evacuation time WHILE prioritizing equity-priority communities; beats rule-based/random. For TRINETRA: the people-at-risk estimate must feed an evacuation layer that also weighs EQUITY (vulnerable Himalayan hamlets), not just total time -> decision-layer completeness + fairness dimension absent from current RL disruption term (#9/#11).

title: GREAT-EER: Graph Edge Attention Network for Emergency Evacuation Responses (Bus Evacuation Orienteering Problem)
relevance_component: evacuation routing + MILP bound
takeaway: Defines NP-hard Bus Evacuation Orienteering Problem (evacuate max people in fixed time); DRL+graph-learning gives sub-second routes, with an MILP formulation to BOUND the optimality gap + estimate how many vehicles meet a quota. Directly relevant to TRINETRA's downstream dispatch: gives a near-real-time, bounded-suboptimality evacuation planner + a way to size vehicle fleets against a people-at-risk count (decision-layer, complements #11).

title: From Perceptions to Decisions: Wildfire Evacuation Decision Prediction with Behavioral-Theory-informed LLMs (FLARE)
relevance_component: evacuee behavior modeling
takeaway: FLARE integrates behavioral theory + CoT reasoning + memory-based RL to predict INDIVIDUAL evacuation decisions (comply vs stay); +20% over theory-informed baselines, cross-event generalizable; notes conflicting individual preferences + implicit mental states. CRITICAL for TRINETRA: its people-at-risk + disruption-cost assume people obey alarms; real compliance is heterogeneous -> alarm policy must model partial/variable compliance, otherwise lead-time and disruption estimates are biased (NEW decision-layer risk, ties #9/#11).

title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Dynamic Multi-Graph Fusion for Evacuation Traffic Prediction (RL-DMF)
relevance_component: evacuation traffic forecasting
takeaway: RL-guided dynamic multi-graph fusion forecasts evacuation traffic flow; 95% acc @1h, 90% @6h on 12 Florida hurricanes incl. unseen Milton 2024; RL-based feature masking for interpretability. For TRINETRA: downstream of an alarm, road capacity/congestion determines achievable lead time; a traffic-forecast layer refines the disruption-cost term + makes the warning actionable (decision-layer realism, #9/#11).

title: Routing algorithms as tools for integrating social distancing with emergency evacuation
relevance_component: evacuation routing (CVRP) RL
takeaway: Casts evacuation as Capacitated Vehicle Routing solved by Deep RL vs Sweep algorithm; DRL gives more efficient routing but the gain cannot offset added constraints (social distancing) as vehicle capacity nears household size. Realistic caution for TRINETRA: RL routing gains are bounded by hard logistical constraints -> don't over-credit the RL layer with capacity it cannot deliver (decision-layer realism, #9/#11).

title: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts for ISAC in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
authors: Zhang; Yu; He; Song; Zhang; Letaief
relevance_component: reliability-aware MoE gating + sparse MoE
takeaway: Each modality gets a dedicated expert; a lightweight gate assigns fusion weights by the INSTANTANEOUS informativeness+reliability of each modality; sparse variant activates a subset of experts to cut compute under energy limits. Two DIRECT lessons for TRINETRA's GMF: (a) gate on per-modality reliability (a snow-obscured InSAR tile or offline CCTV should be down-weighted dynamically, not fused equally); (b) sparse expert activation saves edge energy -> matches offline-first power budget (GMF design upgrade, ties #14 edge cost).

title: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts with Retrieval Augmentation for Protein Active Site Identification (MERA)
authors: Wu; Zhou; Wang; Zhang; Lin; Lv; U; Zheng
relevance_component: Dempster-Shafer reliability fusion
takeaway: Flags that performance DEGRADES when unreliable modalities dominate fusion; fixes it with Dempster-Shafer evidence-theory fusion quantifying modality trustworthiness via belief masses + learnable discounting. For TRINETRA's GMF: a principled, uncertainty-aware alternative to plain gating that explicitly discounts untrustworthy sensors (e.g., decorrelated InSAR, saturated gauge) -> prevents a bad modality from driving a false alarm/miss (GMF robustness, ties conformal/#13 + modality gap).

title: Multimodal Fusion Strategies for Mapping Biophysical Landscape Features
relevance_component: early vs late vs MoE fusion (remote sensing)
