takeaway: Empirically compares Early, Late, and Mixture-of-Experts fusion for thermal+RGB+LiDAR geospatial orthomosaics: macro performance similar (late-fusion AUC 0.698) but PER-CLASS recall differs sharply - early fusion best for some targets, MoE best for others. Grounded remote-sensing evidence for TRINETRA's GMF: no single fusion strategy dominates across hazard classes -> may need class-conditional fusion + must report per-hazard (not just macro) metrics (fusion design + eval discipline, #11).

title: I2MoE: Interpretable Multimodal Interaction-aware Mixture-of-Experts
authors: Xin; Yun; Peng; Choi; Ballard; Chen; Long
relevance_component: interaction-aware interpretable MoE
takeaway: MoE with interaction experts + weakly-supervised interaction losses that explicitly model heterogeneous cross-modal interactions (complement/contradict/independent) + a reweighting model giving sample- and dataset-level interpretation. For TRINETRA's GMF: experts should model whether modalities AGREE or CONTRADICT (e.g., InSAR says stable but CCTV sees movement) rather than assume complementarity, and provide the interpretability regulators/operators need to trust an alarm (GMF design + explainability).

title: Vision-Based Water Level and Flow Estimation
relevance_component: vision river level+velocity (SOTA+stats)
takeaway: Integrates SOTA vision models with statistical modeling + physical priors + robust filtering for water-level and river-surface-velocity estimation; names the real challenges: environmental sensitivity, limited precision, complex site calibration. DIRECTLY validates and bounds TRINETRA's River Eye LSPIV node: vision flow estimation is viable but needs per-site calibration + robust filtering -> the BOM/ops plan must budget calibration + the accuracy claims must reflect these limits (grounds River Eye realism, #8 storm brownout + #14).

title: Unseeded Large Scale PIV measurements accounting for capillary-gravity waves phase speed
relevance_component: LSPIV unseeded bias correction
takeaway: LSPIV measures river surface velocity from image sequences but in UNSEEDED conditions (no floating tracers) capillary-gravity waves travel in all directions and CONTAMINATE the velocity estimate; proposes wavenumber-based discrimination/correction + simple orthorectification. CRITICAL for TRINETRA River Eye: real Himalayan rivers often lack seeding tracers, so raw LSPIV over-/mis-estimates flow unless wave contamination is corrected -> a concrete, un-budgeted accuracy bug in the LSPIV node (NEW River-Eye measurement risk, ties #8).

title: Bayesian estimation of a 1D hydrodynamic model in a tidal river (Lower Seine)
authors: Mendez Rios; Le Coz; Renard; Terraz
relevance_component: rating-curve uncertainty / Manning-Strickler
takeaway: Shows the stage-discharge (rating-curve) relation and Manning-Strickler surface-velocity method BREAK DOWN under unsteady/transient flow; uses a Bayesian-calibrated 1D Saint-Venant model (Mage+BaM!) to quantify friction-coefficient uncertainty. For TRINETRA: converting River Eye surface velocity -> discharge via a static rating curve is unreliable during the exact flash-flood transients that matter; discharge estimates need uncertainty bounds (physics-gate + people-at-risk calibration realism, ties #11/#13).

title: Predicting post-wildfire mudflow onset using ML on multi-parameter experimental data
relevance_component: debris-flow onset timing + I-D sensitivity
takeaway: Flume experiments + ML (MLR/LR/SVC/K-means/PCA) on rain-intensity, slope, water-entry value, grain-size D50 to predict debris-flow onset. KEY empirical findings: fine sand most erodible under LOW-intensity LONG-duration rain; the FIRST 10 MINUTES of high-intensity rain are most critical for discharge+failure. For TRINETRA I-D thresholds (Task C/#15): confirms a single I=aD^-b curve is too coarse - onset depends on grain size + antecedent hydrophobicity + sub-hourly rain structure, so the physics gate should use short (<=10min) rain windows + soil-type conditioning, not just event totals (grounds #3/#15 and the sub-hourly rainfall-input requirement).

title: Quantifying Limits to Detection of Early Warning for Critical Transitions
relevance_component: EWS false-alarm/miss error rates
takeaway: Generic early-warning indicators (rising variance, increased return time) for critical transitions SELDOM characterize their own error rates; a model-based framework quantifies the reliability-vs-sensitivity (false-alarm vs miss) trade-off and shows these error rates can be SEVERE even under favorable assumptions, and vary a lot across datasets. DIRECTLY supports Bug #11 (underpowered eval): TRINETRA's EWS must report expected false-alarm/miss rates with uncertainty, not point metrics on n~5 events; a model-based indicator beats generic variance-based ones (eval discipline + justifies the physics-gate over bare statistical EWS).

title: Deep Learning for Precipitation Nowcasting: A Benchmark and A New Model (TrajGRU)
authors: Shi; Gao; Lausen; Wang; Yeung; Wong; Woo

takeaway: ConvLSTM beats optical-flow nowcasting but its recurrence is location-INVARIANT while real storm motion/rotation is location-variant; proposes TrajGRU (learns location-variant recurrent connections) + a HKO benchmark with a balanced loss + proper evaluation protocol weighting rare heavy-rain pixels. For TRINETRA rainfall input: (a) a cloudburst nowcaster should model location-variant motion; (b) nowcasting eval MUST up-weight rare heavy-rain pixels or metrics are dominated by no-rain - mirrors the imbalance/#1/#11 theme; (c) a documented SOTA baseline to benchmark any TRINETRA rainfall module against (#18 under-benchmarking).

title: Towards physics-informed neural networks for landslide prediction
relevance_component: PINN + Newmark geotechnical retrieval
takeaway: PINN for regional coseismic landslide prediction: adds a Newmark permanent-deformation constraint so the net explicitly RETRIEVES geotechnical parameters from cheap proxy variables, then minimizes loss vs a coseismic inventory; yields both susceptibility AND regional geotechnical-property maps, enabling near-real-time physics-grounded prediction. Direct precedent for TRINETRA's physics-gate+ML coupling and a strong #18 benchmark: shows how to fuse Newmark/infinite-slope physics INTO the learner rather than bolt a gate on afterward (relevant to #3/#16/#17 and the meta-fusion residual-over-physics design). Note: Dahal is the same author as the Task-C 'Dahal-Hasegawa' I-D threshold - trace citation here.

title: Bayesian Updating of Seismic Ground Failure via Causal Graphical Models and Satellite Imagery
relevance_component: causal-graph Bayesian multi-hazard fusion
takeaway: Causal-graph Bayesian network fuses geospatial susceptibility proxies + ShakeMap + damage-proxy-maps (InSAR surface change) to jointly update posteriors of UNOBSERVED landslides/liquefaction/building-damage; stochastic variational inference + graph-pruning for scale; validated on Hokkaido 2018 + Puerto Rico 2020. For TRINETRA fusion layer: a principled, physics-interdependency-aware alternative to the GMF stacked head that (a) propagates uncertainty, (b) handles UNOBSERVED hazard nodes (exactly TRINETRA's sparse-sensor reality), (c) fuses InSAR DPMs with susceptibility - a strong #12/#18 comparator and a candidate structure for correlated-expert fusion (ties GMF multicollinearity risk).

title: Multi-pathology Chest X-ray Classification with Rejection Mechanisms
authors: Aperstein; Tzahar; Gottlib; Verber; Shagan Damti; Apartsin
relevance_component: selective prediction / abstention + per-class thresholds
takeaway: High-stakes multi-LABEL classifier with two abstention mechanisms (entropy-based + confidence-interval-based rejection) + quantile calibration of rejection thresholds using GLOBAL vs CLASS-SPECIFIC strategies; abstaining on uncertain cases defers to human experts and improves the accuracy-coverage trade-off. Maps cleanly onto TRINETRA's alarm head: a multi-hazard (landslide/flood/GLOF co-occurring = multi-label) alarm should ABSTAIN / escalate-to-human when uncertain rather than force a colour, and rejection thresholds should be per-hazard not global - a concrete, calibrated upgrade for the conformal/#13 + threshold/#1 issues and the human-in-the-loop decision layer.

title: Cross-Polarization Fusion of VV and VH SAR Observations for Improved Flood Mapping
relevance_component: VV+VH polarization fusion for flood seg
takeaway: Shows single-polarization SAR flood mapping fails where surface+volume scattering coexist (vegetated/heterogeneous terrain); fusing VV+VH polarizations in a DL segmenter beats either alone on IoU/F1, especially at flood boundaries, under identical training. For TRINETRA: its Sentinel-1 flood/inundation layer should fuse BOTH polarizations, not a single channel - vegetated Himalayan valley floors are exactly the surface+volume-scattering case where single-pol fails; cheap accuracy win + grounds the SAR-input spec (#10 datacube channels, #18).

title: Urban Flood Mapping Using Satellite SAR: Review of Characteristics Approaches and Datasets
relevance_component: SAR flood mapping review + double-bounce pitfall
takeaway: Review of SAR urban-flood mapping: documents that in built-up/complex terrain SAR flood detection is confounded by double-bounce + layover + shadow, and catalogs methods + datasets. For TRINETRA: a map of known SAR failure modes its flood layer will hit in Himalayan towns/settlements (where people-at-risk is highest), plus a dataset/method inventory to benchmark against (#11/#18 under-benchmarking; tempers over-optimistic SAR inundation claims).

relevance_component: MLLM glacial-lake seg + interpretable reasoning
takeaway: First framework coupling an LLM with segmentation for glacial-lake mapping: produces masks PLUS human-interpretable spatial-reasoning text + a GLake-Pos QA dataset; mIoU 87.30 beats CNNs (78.6-79.0), ViTs (69-82), geo-FMs (76-87), reasoning-seg (60-76). For TRINETRA GLOF monitoring: (a) a current SOTA baseline to benchmark its glacial-lake detection against (#18); (b) the natural-language reasoning output is a template for the explainable decision layer regulators need; CAUTION - an MLLM is far too heavy for an offline edge node, so this is a backhaul/cloud-side comparator, not an edge model (#14 edge-latency realism).

title: Fully Autonomous Z-Score TinyML Anomaly Detection on Resource-Constrained MCUs
relevance_component: on-MCU train+infer; concrete footprint/latency
takeaway: Fully on-device (STM32 MCU) TinyML anomaly detector: trains AND infers on the MCU with NO cloud/connectivity, using RMS + lightweight Z-Score thresholds; ~3.3 KB SRAM / 63 KB Flash, tens-of-microseconds inference, P/R=1.00 on a 14-day fridge dataset. HARD REALITY CHECK for TRINETRA #14: genuine edge anomaly detection on a cheap MCU is possible ONLY with tiny statistical models (Z-score/RMS) - NOT the heavy VAD/encoder stack benchmarked on an L40S; this quantifies the achievable edge compute budget and supports a tiered design (tiny on-node screen -> escalate to backhaul). Also an offline-first precedent (no connectivity).

title: Hypothesis Testing and Decision Theoretic Approach for Fault Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks
relevance_component: Neyman-Pearson/Bayes WSN fault vs event
takeaway: Separates NOISE-related measurement error from genuine SENSOR FAULT in WSN event detection, folding error probabilities into optimal detection via Neyman-Pearson and Bayes tests. Directly relevant to TRINETRA's ground-IoT layer: a node reporting an extreme tilt/moisture value may be FAULTY, not sensing a real event - the alarm logic must distinguish the two with a decision-theoretic test (ties the Bayes 5/105 cost framing already in the report) or false alarms spike; supports a formal fault-vs-event test absent from the current pipeline (#8).

title: Searching for Optimal Runtime Assurance via Reachability and Reinforcement Learning
authors: Miller; Zeitler; Shen; Hobbs; Mitra; Schierman; Viswanathan
relevance_component: least-conservative optimal RTA switching
takeaway: Existing runtime-assurance (RTA) switching logics (switch to backup controller) are OVERLY CONSERVATIVE and can STILL violate safety; formulates OPTIMAL RTA as maximizing use of the untrusted controller subject to reachability-based safety, solved with RL. Direct upgrade path for TRINETRA's safety shield (#9): the current fixed hard-override shield is the conservative-RTA case this paper improves on - an optimal/reachability-aware switch would raise alarms only when provably necessary, cutting false alarms while keeping the hard guarantee. Pairs with 2511.21531/2402.00816 (predictive shielding) as the SOTA basis for the shield redesign.

title: Stacked Universal Successor Feature Approximators for Safety in RL (SUSFAS)
authors: Cannon; Garcia; Gresavage; Saurine; Leong; Culbertson
relevance_component: multi-objective safety + backup controllers
takeaway: Real tasks have multi-dimensional objectives (operating cost vs performance vs safety vs availability) irreducible to one scalar reward; SUSFAS = continuous-control universal successor-feature approximation on SAC + a suite of secondary safety (RTA) controllers, improving secondary-objective performance over SAC-with-intervening-RTA. For TRINETRA RL alarm policy (#9): its reward crams miss/FA/lead/disruption into one scalar; successor-feature/multi-objective decomposition lets the policy trade these explicitly and compose with backup safety controllers - a principled alternative to hand-tuned reward weights (complements PBRS 2502.01307).

title: Conformal Prediction for Time Series with Modern Hopfield Networks (HopCPT)
relevance_component: conformal for autocorrelated time series
takeaway: Standard conformal prediction breaks on time series because AUTOCORRELATION violates exchangeability; HopCPT uses a modern Hopfield network to exploit (not just tolerate) temporal structure, with theoretical justification + SOTA on real-world series from 4 domains. Pinpoints exactly why TRINETRA's conformal claim (#13) is an overclaim: its sensor streams are heavily autocorrelated, so vanilla/split-conformal coverage does NOT hold; HopCPT (or similar) is the correct SOTA fix to restore valid intervals for the people-at-risk calibration (#13 fix, pairs with 2406.05405/2511.11567 for missingness+shift).

title: Flow-based Conformal Prediction for Multi-dimensional Time Series
relevance_component: multi-dimensional conformal under non-exchangeability
takeaway: Conformal for time series must (1) exploit correlations in observations+nonconformity scores to beat the exchangeability assumption and (2) build prediction sets for MULTI-DIMENSIONAL outcomes; proposes flow + classifier-free guidance with exact non-asymptotic marginal coverage + finite-sample conditional-coverage bound. For TRINETRA: hazard state is multi-dimensional (deformation, moisture, river level jointly) and non-exchangeable - this gives joint, correlation-aware prediction regions with provable coverage rather than per-variable marginal intervals, a rigorous basis for multi-sensor uncertainty in the fusion head (#13, GMF uncertainty).

title: Dependable Structural Health Monitoring Using Wireless Sensor Networks (DependSHM)
authors: Bhuiyan; G. Wang; J. Wu; J. Cao
relevance_component: faulty sensors corrupt events undetected
takeaway: DependSHM: shows faulty sensors can CORRUPT a structural-health event (e.g., damage) WITHOUT being detected - signals from one faulty node mimic a real damage signature - and builds a distributed fault-detection/tolerance framework under WSN energy/bandwidth limits. This is Bug #8 in another domain: TRINETRA's tilt/geophone/moisture nodes can silently fail and FABRICATE a hazard signature (false alarm) or mask one (miss); the system needs cross-node consistency checks + fault-tolerance, not naive trust of each node (strongly grounds #8 River-Eye brownout + sensor-integrity gap).

title: How Many Independent Samples Does a Satellite Image Contain?
relevance_component: [P4] PROVES C-01: spatial-CV is a theorem not a best-practice
takeaway: Finite-sample upper + matching lower bound: effective sample size of a spatially-correlated image (range r) is Theta(n^2/r^2), NOT n^2; block holdout with separation g=Theta(r*log(n/delta)) achieves optimal generalization; random holdout UNDERESTIMATES CI width by a factor proportional to r. Validated on Landsat-8, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1. For TRINETRA: converts C-01 from a convention into a provable requirement - our tile-withheld spatial-CV with buffer must set the buffer >= correlation range, and any random-split number in the corpus is optimistic by a quantifiable factor. CAVEAT: Gaussian-process stationarity assumption; our terrain correlation range is anisotropic (valleys) -> estimate r per-region. See P4_reading_progress #4.

title: Cost-Sensitive Evaluation for Binary Classifiers
relevance_component: [P4] FORMALIZES C-14: Total Classification Cost as the selection criterion
takeaway: Total Classification Cost (TCC) is the ideal model-selection criterion; weighted-accuracy family and its relation to TCC; metric taxonomy (anti-diagonal / main-diagonal / globally-robust) w.r.t. how a metric tracks TCC across base rates; example-dependent unit costs. For TRINETRA: formalizes 'pick the metric from the cost model' - our primary Value Score is a cost-loss (miss cost >> FA cost), and ranking models across different imbalance ratios by F1/AUC is unsound; report TCC with explicit per-event costs. CAVEAT: binary-only (our WHO/WHEN/people-at-risk are multi-output); costs must be elicited from NDMA/CWC domain experts, not assumed. See P4_reading_progress #5.

title: CLEAR: Robust Evidential Learning Through Latent Consistency
relevance_component: [P4] SUPPORTS C-13: post-hoc fix for confident-but-wrong in sparse/OOD regions
takeaway: Post-hoc method operating on a FROZEN base evidential-deep-learning model; Conflict-Aware Latent Evidence Adjustment: per-sample conflict score C(x) from latent-space geometry, evidence scale s(x)=exp(-delta*C(x)) downweights unsupported (OOD/adversarial) evidence; +8.29/+5.01 OOD/adversarial AUROC, 17.4x faster than retraining; one mechanism covers classification AND regression. For TRINETRA: a concrete post-hoc remedy for C-13 proximity-bias overconfidence (temp-scaling does not fix it) - wrap the risk head's evidence so sparse-region/novel-regime inputs get widened uncertainty into the conformal+shield stack. CAVEAT: needs a base EDL model (adds an evidential head to the forecaster); delta is a tuned hyperparameter; re-measure on our streams. See P4_reading_progress #6.

title: Model Selection for Offline RL: Practical Considerations for Healthcare
relevance_component: [P4] OPERATIONALIZES C-11: iterative RL only if OPE-feasible
takeaway: Offline-RL model-selection pipeline using off-policy evaluation (OPE) as validation; FQE gives the best validation ranking of policies but is compute-heavy; a 2-stage model-selection accelerator; sepsis treatment as safety-critical testbed. Code at github.com/MLD3/OfflineRL_ModelSelection. For TRINETRA: operationalizes the C-11 gate - we may use offline/iterative RL for the alarm policy ONLY if we can rank policies offline with trustworthy OPE; sepsis (irreversible harm, confounded logs) is a direct analogue to alarm decisions. CAVEAT: pre-2022; healthcare domain; OPE itself is high-variance under distribution shift (pairs with 2110.15332 Proximal-RL confounding caveat). See P4_reading_progress #7.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
relevance_component: [P4] FEEDS P14Z + stress-tests C-07/C-02: FMs help ONLY with good covariates
takeaway: 4 TSFM (incl Chronos-2) vs 4 train-from-scratch (incl TimesNet, Informer) on 3 real datasets (ISO-NE, NAU, CAISO) with injected covariate-forecast noise lambda in {0,0.5,1,5}. Chronos-2 is SOTA zero-shot/fine-tuned WHEN future covariates are available and accurately forecast; its advantage DEGRADES as covariate forecasts get noisier; TimesNet is more robust under severe covariate uncertainty. ISO-NE MAE lambda=0: Informer 317.92 / TimesNet 263.98 / Chronos-2 266.25(ZS)/229.82(FT); lambda=5: Informer 1230.29 / TimesNet 707.22 / Chronos-2 1207.72/985.60. For TRINETRA/P14Z: disciplines the zero-shot phase - a TS foundation model is a strong PRIOR only when our driving covariates (rainfall nowcast, upstream level) are themselves reliable; under the noisy monsoon-forecast regime a robust from-scratch model + residual may win. CAVEAT: load-forecasting domain; our covariates are far noisier than ISO load; body-table numbers are FT-PARTIAL (re-verify vs PDF if load-bearing). See P4_reading_progress #8.

title: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Reward Shaping in Reinforcement Learning
relevance_component: [P4] GROUNDS PBRS + flags adaptive-shaping risk (C-10)
takeaway: Review+framework. Static potential-based reward shaping (PBRS) preserves the optimal policy iff the auxiliary term is the discounted difference of a time-invariant potential (Ng 1999). Information-conditioned dynamic shaping R'_k(s,a,s')=R+F_{theta_k}, with mechanism classes C1-C4 and a temporal vocabulary; Section 2.7 enumerates the LIMITS of existing guarantees under episodic tasks/terminal states, partial observability, and multi-agent settings. For TRINETRA: grounds our PBRS doctrine (shape toward physics-plausible early warning without changing the optimal alarm policy) AND warns that once shaping becomes adaptive/learned the optimality guarantee can be lost - keep any shaping potential-based and time-invariant, or prove the exception. CAVEAT: our alarm MDP is partially observed (sensor gaps) -> the §2.6 partial-observability caveat applies directly. See P4_reading_progress #9.

title: Boundary-Aligned Contribution Routing for Robust Optical-SAR Object Detection
relevance_component: [P4] C-08 mechanism: more modalities != better; route before mixing
takeaway: Optical-SAR fusion with task-conditioned contribution routing applied BEFORE the first cross-modal feature-value mixing (Feature Router near input + Dual-Statistic Semantic Router for dual-backbone late fusion); learned from detection supervision ALONE (no utility labels/quality labels/reconstruction/distillation). Results on M4-SAR, SpaceNet6-OTD: full-input mAP50 +0.5..5.9pt; MISSING-modality mAP50 +7.6..41.6pt over modality-dropout baselines; negative-transfer rate -12.7pp; routing-weight vs leave-one-modality-out utility Spearman 0.45-0.66. For TRINETRA: direct C-08/CR-07 mechanism - 'presence of a modality does not guarantee beneficial fusion'; our GMF should gate each sensor's contribution by learned task-utility before fusing, so a corrupted/stale SAR tile cannot drag the alarm. CAVEAT: object-detection task (ours is risk regression/alarm); re-derive routing on our modalities; Spearman 0.45-0.66 = routing is a proxy for utility, not utility itself. See P4_reading_progress #10.

takeaway: Peer-reviewed PINN for regional coseismic-landslide susceptibility: an intermediate constraint solves for Newmark permanent slope deformation; the NN explicitly retrieves geotechnical parameters from common proxy variables, then minimizes BCE against the coseismic landslide inventory; also outputs regional maps of expected geotechnical properties. title: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? (RA-Bench)
authors: Liang; Ma; Zhou; Wan; Chen; Mei; et al.
relevance_component: [P4] LIFE-SAFETY ANCHOR for C-16/WS2: no deepfake detector generalizes
takeaway: RA-Bench: 17,886 videos = 1,830 real-video anchors across 10 social-risk categories + 16,056 generated clips from 9 generators (4 open + 5 closed). Evaluated 7 traditional detectors, 10 zero-shot multimodal models (3 review settings), 2 fine-tuned MLLMs: NONE of the three detector families generalizes consistently; videos that mislead humans are also hard for detectors; social dissemination makes detection HARDER; source-level patterns stable across seeds. For TRINETRA: hard evidence for Rule 19/C-16 - deepfake/AI-video and zero-shot media signals are LOW-TRUST advisory inputs into GMF+conformal+shield, NEVER an autonomous alarm or verification oracle; the misinformation workstream (WS2) must assume detectors fail on exactly the crisis content that matters. CAVEAT: detection benchmark (not a system we build); fast-moving generators -> any detector we cite will age; 63pp FT-PARTIAL (body tables partially captured). See P4_reading_progress #12.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting of InSAR Ground Deformation in Eastern Ireland
relevance_component: [P4] C-03/WS8: InSAR forecast design + persistence-trap + two-baseline
takeaway: Sparse PS-InSAR points -> dense spatio-temporal tensor -> hybrid CNN-LSTM for single-step-ahead deformation forecasting; benchmarked against LightGBM and LASSO on Sentinel-1 over eastern Ireland; input window Tin=300 steps; SHAP (TreeExplainer) feature attribution. For TRINETRA WS8: a direct InSAR-deformation-forecast blueprint (tensorize sparse PS points, forecast, SHAP-explain) + reinforces C-03 (learn a residual beyond persistence) + the two-baseline rule (GBDT+LASSO). See P4_reading_progress #13.

authors: Holmberg; Pokhrel; Zoch; Ioup; Pathak; et al.

For TRINETRA WS1: a template for a cheap physics-surrogate so we can run ENSEMBLE flood forecasts inside the Kaggle budget - learn a surrogate of a calibrated hydraulic model, then ensemble it. title: LoMETab: Beyond Rank-1 Ensembles for Tabular Deep Learning
relevance_component: [P4] C-02 CURRENCY (2026): DL-vs-GBDT gap narrowed to a TIGHT CLUSTER, GBDT still exceptionally strong
takeaway: Tabular-DL method paper that OPENS with the current (May 2026) consensus: 'recent tabular benchmarks increasingly show a tight performance CLUSTER rather than a clear hierarchy' among GBDT, attention-based, and implicit ensembles (TabM); 'GBDTs remain exceptionally strong', while 'simple MLP-based tabular models can be surprisingly competitive, often matching/outperforming more complex attention/retrieval architectures.' Method: LoMETab = rank-r generalization of multiplicative implicit ensembles W_k=W(1+A_kB_k^T); member-wise loss (avg per-member task loss) following TabM; benchmarked on 37 source datasets / 77 eval tasks (TabM + TabZilla), baselines sourced identically from Gorishniy et al.; proves rank-r strictly enlarges BatchEnsemble class for r>=2. For TRINETRA: the 2026 CURRENCY CHECK for C-02 - the parsimony result has NOT reversed; the DL-vs-GBDT gap has merely NARROWED to a tight cluster where GBDT is still exceptionally strong and the competitive neural models are the SIMPLE ones (not big attention nets). Confirms 'GBDT baseline mandatory, simple-first' and warns against complex attention/retrieval tabular nets. CAVEAT: general-tabular benchmark (not hazard/spatial), no spatial-CV (C-01 still applies on OUR data); plateau = small absolute diffs, re-measure under cost-loss (DC-02). NEW (genuine P4 15th; FT-PARTIAL arxiv.org/html, body tables pruned). See P4_reading_progress #17.
